maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Since confederation $83,000.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: How much by this government ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I have not the figures here.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: How much more will be spent ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: We have not undertaken to let any new contracts next yeaT.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Was there no plan made?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
This is very necessary work. We could stop right now and have done good work in the way of improving the harbour, but there is. other work to be done if we choose to do it. We have not decided yet to do any further woTk.
Riviere Saguenay-wharf on northeast side of Riviere aux Vases, $800.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Is the hon. minister sure this is not for a municipal bridge ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I have no information that it is intended for a bridge. The proposed wharf will be 180 by 20, the outer block 30 by 30. Depth of water at low tide, seven feet. Total length, 210 feet. That does not sound much like a bridge, and I am sure my hon. friend need have no fears on the subject.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: What is there there?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: This is a small village, with two cheese factories and two stores. The only market is Chicoutimi, and the only communication is by water.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: How much will the wharf cost?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: About $7,000.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Is it a navigable stream?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: The Saguenay?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: This is not on the Saguenay. This is on the Riviere aux Vases.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: No, this is on the Saguenay.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Is a depth of seven feet sufficient for the Saguenay boats?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: It is enough for the boats that ply on that part of the river, but not for the big boats.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Is it above or below Chicoutimi?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: It is six miles above Ste. Anne village, and above Chicoutimi.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Are these wharfs built on piles?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: No.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: What are they made of?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
Cribwork.
Riviere St. Franpois-landing pier at St. Francois du Lac, on the west side of river, $8,000.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: How much was voted for this last parliament?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: The work was done by day's labour, was it, not?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Yes. This, I think, is in almost exactly the same position as the other we were discussing.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Twice as bad, for it cost double the amount.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I was in hopes it was not half as bad.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: When did the appropriation run out?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I will get that information and bring it down with the other.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Strange, is it not, that all these cases occur in the county of Ya-maska? It is a very close constituency, and the majority to the credit of the Liberal candidate is small.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Still, it is enough.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: These two wharfs may have had something to do with making it enough -just enough.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Here is another case of the minister spending $5,000 by day's work. Did he get an order in council to authorize it?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: No. I did not think the expenditure would reach $5,000.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: But he knows it now; does he propose to get an order in council for the prosecution of the work?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: The work is about completed.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: What made it so expensive? What was the estimate?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: It cost for wharf and right of way $10,000.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: From whom was the right of way purchased?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: A gentleman by the name of Cocher.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: When was it bought?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: August 26, 1908.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: When was Mr Cocher paid?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I presume, about that time. The order in council was passed on the date I have given. The payment would be made through the Justice Department, and I have no memorandum of it.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: What is the law that guides the minister in this matter?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I will send for the statutes.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Let me put the question: When the expense is not over $5,000, the minister can have it done by day's labour, but, in order to do that, must have an order in council? And if it is over $5,000, does the law provide that he has no option but to do the work by tender and contract?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I think thq hon. member is in error.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: The minister should have direct knowledge on that point to aid that conscience of his.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: What is the penalty if the minister violates the law?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: One penalty is to get raked over the coals by hon. gentlemen opposite. And there is nothing much worse than that; it hurts me so much.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: This seems to be an aggravated case. The minister asks $2,000 for a public work, and spends the $2,000, and then spends $8,000 illegally after the other is exhausted. There seems to be something about public works in Yamaska which causes the minister to drop the usual precautions.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
While I am waiting for the statutes to be brought, perhaps we could go on with other items.
Riviere St. Jacques (Laprairie)-ice piers near mouth on River St. Lawrence, $260.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Is that the price of the pier?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: This is a balance due. The contract was for $7,023.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Is this the same kind of ice pier as Annapolis is to have to chain its ice down?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Not exactly the same.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: No suggestion of a bridge in this item?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
No.
Ste. Anne des Monts-harbour improvements at mouth of Grand Riviere Ste. Anne, $1,100.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: What has been done there?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: This is for a combined dam, training pier and brush and stonework protection extending from one side of the river to a small rocky islet. Then there will be some new dredging to keep the channel open to a depth of about five feet at low water.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Is that for the purpose of directing the movement of the ice ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: No, this is not an ice pier, this is to keep the channel open for the entrance and departure of small vessels. The total cost is $17,750.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Why was this done by day labour instead of by contract ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Give us the law now.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
This was a class of work that could be better done by day labour, in the opinion of the engineer. The law will be found in the first Revised Statutes of Canada, chapter 39:
36. Whenever any works are to he executed under the direction of any department of the government, the minister having charge of such department should invite tenders by public advertisement for the execution of such works, except in cases,-
(a)	of pressing emergency in which delay would be injurious to the public interest; or,
(b)	in which from the nature of the work it can be more expeditiously and economically executed by the officers and servants of the department; or,
(c)	where the estimated cost of the work is less than five thousand dollars and it appears to the ministers in view of the nature of the work, that it is not advisable to invite tenders.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I think there is a provision defining the emergency, is there not ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I am not aware of anything else in the statute bearing on that question. 1 may say to my hon. friend that my view has been that in cases where the work is important and likely to involve an expenditure of over $5,000, I have felt it my duty to go to council. But except in cases where, in the opinion of the engineer, the work is not likely to cost a great deal of money, and it can be done more expeditiously and more economically by day's work, in some cases I have not gone to council. In some cases we are not bound to go to council, but I have usually done so.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: How much of this $17,000 has gone into the construction of the approach to this wharf ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
I may have had in my memorandum last year a reference to the approach, I have none with me at present.
I do not see why I would have used the expression including the approach, because I do not see what approach there would be.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Evidently the minister thought he had good reason for using that term last year. Would the minister make further inquiries ?-'because I would like to know what proportion has been expend- . ed in the approach that will be required for this work?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I think I must have been misreported last year, or else I used the expression without warrant.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.

speechtext: I understand that the slipping away of the old wharf is equivalent to a loss of $125,000, inasmuch as it costs that amount to put it back in a good condition again. What did the minister discover to be the reason for the loss of the wharf at Sorel?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: The reason was the peculiarity of the soil in the river bed. There is a good deal of quicksand, and the wharf as originally constructed was not designed apparently to withstand the shifting of the quicksand. I think the first wharf was built upon piles and evidently the soil slipped from the bank. There was a landslide and it carried the pile wharf into the river. We have changed the design. We have excavated a foundation for the wharf and put in a large quantity of stone as a lower foundation and upon that we are building crib work. The engineers believe that the present design, which has been studied very carefully, will do for a wharf which will be permanent in character.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.

I understand that there is a great loss to the government every year by reason of these wharfs being swept away along the St. Lawrence. Has it occurred to the department that it would be better and cheaper to carve slips into the river bank than to extend the docks out where they will be caught and carried away by the ice? In other countries, I understand, they cut slips in the banks of the rivers instead of sticking wharfs out into the water where in the spring they are carried away by the ice. They had to change the design entirely and build on crib work. I would assume, -until I had some evidence to the contrary beyond mere hearsay, that the resident engineer who was responsible for the designing of the plan, was familiar with the local conditions, and that circumstances arose which were not anticipated.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: We would like to have the name of the engineer who drew the plan. It would not take the hon. gentleman more than two minutes to get it.
