COMMON a

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I recognize the importance of Collingwood harbour. The business there has increased rapidly and there is no doubt that further improvements are very much needed; but it must be borne in mind that we have already expended in a comparatively few years pretty close to $1,000,000 in Collingwood and we have made it a good harbour. But at the same time we must recognize that the business is congested and that there is necessity for further improvements. The channel needs straightening, there are some edges of rock to be taken off and some deepening to be done. The matter is engaging my careful attention. I do not know just what we can do this year, we have many demands from a great many sections of the country and my general dredging vote is very small, I am sorry to say.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
In this connection I would point out the importance of the question of lake transportation. I notice that in the estimates the knife has been put very deeply into the works appertaining to transportation, especially on the great lakes. I mentioned to the House once before this session that the works at Fort William and Port Arthur were being carried out in accordance with the recommendation of the Royal Commission on Transportation. There is one weak link ini the chain, the points on the lower end of the lakes. I do not think the government recognize that the increase in the number of steamers and barges in our lake fleet will necessitate the construction of fully half a mile of new dock accommodation at the lower end of the lakes every year. Each of these ships is from 300 to 500 feet long, and they must have discharging accommodation. We should consider the advisability of making ample provision at the various ports on the lakes, for their accommodation. It will be only ten or fifteen years until we will not have enough harbours for that traffic. I find in the statistical report of lake commerce given by Col. Davis of the corps of engineers of the United States navy and also in the report by the American section of the International Waterways Commission, that the number of Canadian steel steamers in that trade in 1907 was 108. The number has now increased by about 8 or 10, making 115. The registered tonnage in 1907 was 92,224 tons and the value of this tonnage was $7,648,000. The average cost of carriage from the head of the lakes per ton mile to the lower end was -08 cents. I am giving these figures with a view to showing just what advantage the public are deriving from the work carried on by this government and the necessity for these improvements. The total tonnage carried, according to the American statistics, was 2,747,750 tons. About an equal amount is carried from Port Ar-Mr. J. A. CURRIE.
thur and Fort William in American bottoms, making a tonnage of nearly 5,000,000 tons a year from the head of the lakes to American and Canadian ports. The average trip to the American ports would be about 827 miles, but many of the Canadian ships go as far as Montreal, and the average trip will be about 1,000 miles, and at an average cost of transportation of -06 cents per ton mile. The saving on the thousand mile trip over rail transportation will be 31 i cents per ton.
Take that saving on 5,000,000 tons a year, and you will find that the farmers of our Northwest actually save $1,775,000 per annum on the cost of transport of their products to Montreal by water, as compared with what they would have to pay for haulage by rail. Within the last two or three years Montreal has been getting the bulk of the grain traffic for Europe, which is due to our good harbours and deep waterways. Taking up to-day's newspaper I find that the Americans are endeavouring to take the grain trade away from Canada through American ports and are taking steps to cut the through rates on the American trunk lines. With this end in view they have cut about a cent a bushel on grain to the sea-board all around. It is up to us to see that we do not lose the advantage we have gained after many years of struggle and the expenditure of enormous amounts of public money. The fact that on the other side of the line they are endeavouring to take the trade away from us should make us all the more determined to keep it and if necessary spend a little more money for that purpose. Such money will be well spent because the expenditure will accrue to the benefit ol the Northwest, not only as regards the people there now but the millions who will be there ten or fifteen years hence. It is estimated that the canals at Sault Ste. Marie will not be able inside of ten years to accommodate the amount of traffic requiring to go through them. I know that many hon. members really cannot realize the enormous amount of traffic which comes down through that country, and by which the ports of Montreal, St. John and Halifax are benefited. But if that tonnage goes through Buffalo and Erie, the earnings on the lower end of the tonnage, which now benefits the people of eastern Canada, will be lost to Canada. What that means can be realized when the saving of 31 cents a ton amounts to nearly $2,000,000. I feel satisfied that the minister recognizes the importance of this, but I wish to impress it upon the House, and more especially on his colleagues, who are not in touch with the transportation problems of this country. Tne hon. Minister of Railways and Canals knows the tremendous growth of this trade. I can remember when you could count all the ships en-

gaged in it in Canada on the fingers of your hands, but to-day we have over 100 steel vessels carrying that traffic. I trust the government will see fit to increase the expenditure this year on those lower lake terminals. I know that the question of expenditure on the port of Montreal will come up, but as a Canadian, living far from Montreal, I would be satisfied to vote in favour of making Montreal and St. John free harbours. That is the only way in which we can keep our supremacy. This year the estimates for the province of Ontario on the upper lakes has been cut down over $1,000,000 in the case of harbours and other improvements to navigation. I know that the government left the door possibly a little too wide open in its policy last year on account of the elections, but after all the cut,
I think, is a little too deep, especially in view of the fact that other departments of the government have not been quite so economical. We all recognize that the Minister of Public Works has great difficulties to meet, we all know that he has to try and disarm with his pleasant, sunny smile those who are urging expenditures on him, but I think he should rather exercise his diplomatic arts on his colleagues and make them give a little more money in order that these works may be carried out and that the spout be not too small at any particular end. The port of Montreal should be looked after, the whole chain of transportation should be looked after. It is that chain which has given us the supremacy. Instead of spending money on visionary projects for diverting the traffic from Montreal and these other ports to Hudson bay and elsewhere, we should rather spend our means on practical objects, and then, if we have anything more to spend, use it on these future possibilities.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: The hon. gentleman apparently has fallen into the impression that our harbours in the Georgian Bay district are insufficient to take care of the traffic. I would remind him that one dock, 500 feet in length, capable of accommodating an ordinary steamer, can handle at least 10,000 tons a day. In fact boats carrying ten thousand tons are frequently unloaded in less than seven hours time.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: What kind of freight?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Ore.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: There is no ore coming from the west.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: It will unload ten thousand tons of grain in six or seven hours and on that basis twenty docks would handle 50,000,000 tons during the eight months of navigation.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: My hon. friend should take a trip and find out whether he could handle 10,000 tons of package freight in seven hours at any of these ports. If he can do that, he ought to take out a patent, and he would make a fortune. That freight is all handled by hand, and to handle ten thousand tons by hand is slow work.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
I was not aware that package freight comes from the west.
I was referring to the grain trade.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: There happens to be an immense quantity of package freight for the west and from the west. I would endorse every word of my hon. friend from Simcoe (Mr. Currie). I have lived on the Georgian bay for some fifty years, and watching the development from year to year, I know the growing importance of these works and the urgent need for the expenditure of money. No doubt in the future all these ports will be overtaxed. Although the accommodation there is moderately fair to-day, in the future it will not be sufficient for the needs. With the increasing number of railways reaching the Georgian bay, it becomes absolutely necessary to have these harbours made suitable for handling freight. You may unload a boat very rapidly with grain, but there are times when it is a very slow process. At Owen Sound frequently you will see the place crowded, and I presume it is the same in Collingwood and Midland and in all these ports on the Georgian bay.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I do not object to my hon. friends pointing out what they think ought to be done in the future, but it would be a graceful thing if they would recognize what we have done in the very recent past.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: We do.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
I am very glad to hear it. I think that this government is entitled to the greatest possible credit for its recognition of the transportation needs of the country and more especially of the great opportunities which exist for the development of trade between the western shores of Lake Superior and the ports' of eastern Canada by way of the great lakes. We have done a great deal in the past. We have done all that the government could be expected to do. Just consider what has been done at Port Arthur. We are engaged in deepening the harbour, we have al-readv deepened it to 22 feet, and our plan provides for 25 feet so as to give accommodation to the largest lake steamers, which can go to any port on the western shores of Lake Superior, whether American or Canadian ports.
We are building a great breakwater, which, ultimately, will be made two or three miles in extent, so as to afford not only a
revised edition

safe harbour but one in which the shipping will be moved with the greatest economy and convenience. At Fort William, in addition to the terminals of the Canadian Pacific, we are engaged in a large scheme of deepening and widening the Mission and Kaministiquia rivers. Here also we are providing a depth of twenty-five feet. We are making a turning) basin with an area of thirty-two acres, with a view to giving every possible facility for the handling of vessels. We are also building a long revetment wall which will be of great benefit to the shipping in the harbour. Of course the Canadian Pacific Railway, the Grand Trunk Railway, and the Canadian Northern are doing their part, but the government is co-operating with these railways to the utmost extent. I think my hon. friend (Mr. J. A. Currie) ought to realize that the government and the country is dealing in a broad spirit with these harbours when it is providing, notwithstanding the present conditon of the revenues, $600,000 for improvements at these ports on the western shore of Lake Superior during the coming season. That is a large sum to spend and it will be spent to the best advantage. The result will be that, before long, there will be terminal facilities at the western end of Lake Superior which will not be surpassed by any port in the world. I have seen the plans of these railway companies, and I know what our plans are. The terminals are being made on a broad and comprehensive scale. We are working to a definite plan and with the determination to make these ports all they ought to be. Our aim is to provide that any lake vessel which can enter the harbour of Duluth or Chicago shall be able to enters the harbours of Fort William and Port Arthur. What we want is that our harbours shall be equal if not superior to those on the United States side of the line. We realize that for many years, the grain traffic of the west has been going to the port of Buffalo and the Atlantic ports of the United States. It is much to be regretted that as much as 18,000,000 bushels of Canadian grain passed through the port of Buffalo last year and was lost to the eastern Canadian ports. We are seeking to remedy that. That is our aim, and we hope that, before long, the whole grain trade of the west, as well as the other trade of that country, will pass through Canadian channels and through Canadian seaports to the markets of the old country. I believe we shall succeed. Now come to the eastern shores of the Georgian bay. The hon. member says that we ought to pay more attention to the development there than we have done. We have spent money in the improvement of the harbours of Parry Sound, Collingwood-and I may say right here that, at Collingwood, Mr. PUGSLEY.
we have spent about $1,000,000. The gentleman who represented that riding before my hon. friend (Mr. J. A. Currie) was persistent in putting forward the claims of Collingwood and he got great recognition of those claims.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: He made a lot of sacrifices to get it.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I am not prepared to say that the country made any sacrifice. I am not prepared to say that the expenditure was not a wise one. It has greatly increased the facilities for carrying the trade on the great lakes.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I suppose the hon. gentleman (Mr. Pugsley) is aware that the work was undertaken virtually in partnership with the town-the town paid its share ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: It is always well when the municipal authorities show their faith m the future sufficiently to put their money ln. it-it is good evidence that they have faith in the town. And, no doubt, it made it easier for the gentleman who represented the constituency to win the recognition he did of Collingwood's claims. We have improved the harbours of Owen Sound, Midland, Southampton, Goderich, Sarnia, Mea-ford, Penetanguishene and Depot Harbour -all ports on Georgian Bay and Lake Huron, and all giving signs of being capable of doing large business with our Canadian west. Take Goderich, for example" it is perfectly wonderful how the trade of that port has increased. From only two or three millions of bushels of grain which came there a few years ago, the trade increased so that, last season, 10,000,000 bushels of Canadian grain were brought into Goderich harbour. Goderich bids fair to become a great distributing point for the grain trade of the west. We have spent a good deal of money there and are asked to spend more. We hope we shall be able to spend more. Our attention was called to what seemed to open up a greater possibility than ever before of developing trade through Canadian ports by means of the railways, and these new harbours of Tiffin and Victoria. What will it mean when these railways are constructed? It will mean that one locomotive will haul forty cars of grain in a trainload, instead of fifteen or twenty cars as at present, thus reducing the cost of hauling grain by fifty per cent. I mention these things to show that we have not been dealing in a niggardly way in the expenditures we have made in the development of transportation between the east and west.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
I know that a very strong effort is being made by the two transportation companies to have all the money spent at Tiffin and Victoria harbour. But I want to point out that fully forty per cent of the grain that comes from the northwest

is ground in mills in Ontario and through this adjacent country. I will warrant that fully fifty per cent of the grain that came through the elevator at Goderich was absorbed before it reached Montreal, or, at the very least, before it reached the maritime provinces. When we consider the enormous quantity of grain coming down from the west, it is evident that the portion that goes into local consumption will afford business for other harbours than Tiffin and Victoria. For that reason, I do not see why making terminals at these two points for the through traffic should prevent a little money being spent at other places that have given evidences of their good faith and their belief in themselves and in their public woTks. And, after all said and done, after the work at Tiffin and Victoria harbour is all finished, the same trouble will exist as before-there will not be sufficient dockage. The hon. gentleman who quoted figures about the vast quantity of tonnage that can be got from the hold of a vessel in a short time, had in mind the work at the docks of Cleveland and Lorraine, where they will run fourteen buckets holding ten tons each into the hold of a vessel to be loaded at once with iron ore. These vessels that traverse the lakes spend fully fifty per cent of their time loading and unloading. Sometimes they have to wait three days for their cargo at the head of the lakes, and sometimes four or five days at the south end of the lake to have their cargo discharged. The minister has told us how $600,000 is to be spent by the government in the development of Fort William and Port Arthur:	But the railway companies
and elevator companies, I understand, are spending $2,000,000 in improving their grain handling facilities there. The only reason why I dwell on the importance of Georgian bay ports in this:	If you turn to the minister's own report you will find an extract from an American authority showing that the vessels the Americans are employing are vessels 500 and 600 feet long and carrying 10,000 to 12,000 tons at a load. It is important for us to keep our seaports going in the winter time, and for that reason we should have large storage elevators at this side of the lake as well as large terminals at the other, so that grain can be hurried down in the winter months through the natural channels, for instance, to St. John. A large quantity now goes to Portland that should go to St. John, or Halifax, or other ports on the eastern shores of Canada. There is no reason why one pound of this tonnage should go out of this country except through Canadian ports.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
The minister thought he was doing a good deal at the head of Lake Superior in making these harbours suitable for ingress and egress of the largest boats from the east or from the west. But 1041
I want to draw his attention to the fact that the same boats go to the south shore of the Georgian bay. Boats carrying 250,000 bushels of grain, and that is about the ordinary cargoes, come down the Georgian bay, and the harbours must be equally as deep and as good on the Georgian bay as they are at Port Arthur and Fort William, though they may not require as much space. They want just as great a depth of water and equally good facilities for loading and unloading. The minister says he thinks they have done very well in providing and spending $600,000 on these harbours at Fort William, Port Arthur and other harbours. But does he think, when they are spending over a million dollars on that Newmarket ditch, what that sum of money would do for these very harbours we are speaking of, and that whereas, in the one instance, the money is absolutely thrown away, in the other instance it is very much needed. Tf there is a shrinkage in the revenue and it becomes necessary to curtail expenditure, we would expect a wise government to curtail expenditure on useless proposals, and use all the money available in places where it is very much needed, like these harbours on the Georgian bay. The money is verv much needed at Port Arthur and Foit William. A large share of that grain, as my hon. friend from Sim-coe (Mr. J. A. Currie) says, is hoisted into elevators on the south shore of the Georgian bay, and in the winter it is distributed to the mills that grind all the time. Consequently these improvements are required in these harbours. _ Meaford is a fairly good harbour, but it is not equal to the needs. There is only room for one boat to go in at a time. Owen Sound is a better haTbour than Meaford, but in neither is there anything like the depth of water that is sometimes needed. Then Collmg-wood has a fairly good harbour compared with what it was years ago; but the grain growing trade of the country will outstrip its conveniences in the near future, So all these harbours call for constantly m-creasing expenditure to keep them up _ to the development of the trade that is going on from year to year.
Little Current-improvements of Northern channel ih Georgian bay, $82,000.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
That is to pay the balance' due on the contract for the current year. The work is being done on what is called the inside channel of Little Current, between Manitoulin island and the mainland. It is dredging and blasting rock.
Harbours, rivers and bridges-general repairs and improvements, $5,500.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
I desire to call attention to a matter which I think I may pro->erl" mention under this item. Some days ago I put a question on the Order Paper in reference to the Wolfe Island canal, and I was informed that the Department of

Public Works could not get any information in reference to that matter. Now Mr. Chairman, this Wolfe Island canal was constructed over 50 years ago, and therefore there may be an excuse for the department not being able to find information in reference to it. It was in use up to about 20 years ago, since which time it has not been in use. I want to draw the minister's attention to the following circumstances. There is a bridge across that canal which is necessary to the people living on Wolfe island. That bridge has got to be .reconstructed or repaired, I think a new bridge will have to be built, and naturally the people of Wolfe island would like to get assistance in rebuilding it. They have applied to the department for assistance, and have been refused. They have also asked to be allowed to shorten the spans of that bridge, and have been told that they must not fill in on either side of the canal. Now, it does seem to me, and I think it must seem to this committee, that it is a hardship that those people can neither shorten the span of the bridge, nor can they get any assistance to rebuild it, nor can they make any use whatever of the canal, which, as I said, has not been used for over 20 years. I want to ask the Minister of Public Works if he will either grant some assistance to the people of Wolfe island in rebuilding that bridge, if he desires that the span of the bridge shall not be shortened, or that he will leave it to the council of that municipality to exercise their own judgment in filling in and shortening the span as they think proper. I am only asking what is reasonable, namely, that he will either permit the council of Wolfe island to exercise their option in shortening up the span and construct a shorter bridge, or if he desires that the bridge be not shortened, that he will grant some assistance to the people of that municipality in building a bridge of the same length as the old one.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Who constructed the bridge in the first place ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
That is a question I asked the Minister of Public Works some time ago, and he was unable to answer me.
I am sure that the municipalities through which it. runs contributed by way of bonus to the construction of that canal, but I cannot say how much. I am also under the impression that the Dominion government, or the provincial government, gave some assistance, although I am not sure as to that. I have been told by residents of the island that the Dominion government claims jurisdiction over the canal, claims authority to say that the islanders shall not shorten the span of the bridge. If they do claim that jurisdiction, it seems to me they .ought to help in constructing a new bridge across the canal.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I am sure my hon. friend would not ask me to build a bridge at Wolfe island, which is wholly within the province of Ontario; I do not see upon what ground I could ask parliament for authority to do that. But, with regard to giving permission to the municipality to shorten the span, as at present advised, I do not see any objection to doing that. If the public have not been using it for the purpose of navigation for a number of years past I do not see any objection to making the span narrower. I think I am quite safe in saying that if the municipality will send the plans to my department, showing the span which they would like to have shortened, their request will receive favourable consideration. The matter has not come before me, but I shall certainly give to any such request my most favourable consideration because I recognize that anything that can be done, without interfering with navigation or interfering with the public interest, which would reduce to the municipality the cost of repairing the bridge, ought to be done.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Of course, the hon. gentleman says that this canal is entirely within the province of Ontario. I do not know that it differs very materially in that respect from the Rideau canal or the Newmarket canal. If this canal was constructed by the government originally and if the government of to-day claim jurisdiction over it, I do not see any reason why the government should not construct the bridge across that canal as well as eonstruct a bridge across the Rideau canal.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: The government, as far as I am aware, does not claim any jurisdiction over the canal. If it were used for the purpose of navigation we would have the same control as we do over any navigable water. It would only be in that respect that we would have jurisdiction over it. But we have never claimed any jurisdiction or ownership over it. As far as I can learn the canal was built long before confederation, but concerning the question as to who built it there seems to be no definite information.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: It was built by private parties.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: The Dominion government sent a dredge there to deepen it not many years ago.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Perhaps so.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
When we were discussing wharfs in Quebec last night or the night before, I referred to the fact that in the townships of Wolfe Island and Howe Island they have several wharfs there that have been built by private parties and that they have no other means of getting a market than by steamer. I know that the people of Wolfe island can only get to King-

ston or Gananoque by steamer and that the wharfs were constructed on Wolfe island and Howe island by private parties. I think that when the government is building wharfs all over the country the townships of Howe Island and Wolfe Island should also have some assistance from the government.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: The Public Works Department build wharfs on the property of private parties.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: No.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I think I can give an instance to the minister.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: No

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: On the St. Lawrence river below Cornwall.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I know the island you mean.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: There is an island owned entirely by a private party.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: The hon. gentleman says that the government had built a wharf there on private property. It is not the case. Adjoining the government property there is private property, but the wharf is built on government property.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: The wharf is built on property there that belongs to a private individual.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: The land adjoining the wharf belongs to a private individual.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: But the whole island belongs to a private party. I do not suppose that the government bought the land upon which the wharf is.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Yes, they did. Would the hon. gentleman expect the government to buy the whole island?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: No, but I want to say to the minister that they simply built that wharf there for the convenience of a private individual. It was built entirely for his purposes.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: No, it was built as a harbour of refuge for the boats plying on the river.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: It is simply a pleasure resort owned by a private individual.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Another case of misinformation.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
The minister knows well enough that that was an island owned by a private individual who had a wharf there before and the government rebuilt it for him. In this case that my hon. friend from Frontenac (Mr. Edwards) is speaking about, I remember that last year or the year before a deputation came down and wanted assistance of the kind to
which my hon. friend has referred. I know the place well. The government practically-took possession of the canal, and the fact that they had been dredging and improving it made it necessary to provide a more expensive bridge. It also made it necessary to have a swing bridge that will cost much more than would be required if it were simply a stationary bridge. If the canal were dredged out there is no doubt that the route would be a great deal shorter between Kingston and Cape Vincent than going around by the upper part of the island as they have to do at present.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: The hon. member for Kingston (Mr. Harty). if I understood him correctly a minute ago, interjected a remark that this canal was built entirely by private parties.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I always understood so.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: My information is not the same as that of the hon. member for Kingston. He may be right but I do not think he is. While a company constructed the canal I think I am quite correct in saying that the municipality of Wolfe Island contributed by way of a bonus to the building of the canal.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: They may have.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: And I think the county of Frontenac also contributed something. Here was a canal which was constructed, we will say, by a private company which the municipality of Wolfe Island contributed to and which has been out of use for something like twenty years, a canal from which the municipality, is getting no benefit whatever, has not for a great many years, and I think it is most unfair that this useless canal should be the means of imposing extra expense on that municipality. I think I am quite within my rights and that the people there are quite within their rights in asking a contribution from the government towards the construction of that bridge or that it may be left to them to shorten the span as they may see fit. I think the facts are that this company failed to carry on the canal and that the canal passed into the hands of the government. I am rather confirmed in that idea because of the fact that the government within the last twenty-five years, at all events, expended money in dredging that canal. I maintain that if the government claim ownership over this canal they should construct the bridge entirely.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: My department does not claim any ownership over it.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Whether you claim ownership or not I think the government is the owner of the canal.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I do not see how this government can be the owner of it.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: If you were not the owner why did you spend money on it? Why was dredging done upon it?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: We spend money on many rivers simply because we are requested by the people to do so to improve navigation. We do not own the bed of the river; we have no title and no jurisdiction over the foreshore so far as I know. If anything was done by the provincial government before confederation which gave us title to this canal, the bed of it and the soil of it would all be owned by the Ontario government because it would not pass at confederation to the control of the federal government All that the Federal government has is control of navigation on navigable waters.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I presume that in exercising that right over navigable waters the federal government would not allow the municipalities of Wolfe Island to shorten the span of the bridge?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: That would be the reason; if it is not useful for navigation that reason would not exist.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: The claims of the municipalities there should receive the consideration of the government. There is a large amount of trade passing to and from these islands to Kingston and across the line, and as it seems to be the policy of the government to build wharfs and dredge harbours, the older settled parts of the country should receive consideration as well as the newly settled districts. ,

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
Two sessions ago I brought to the notice of the government the urgent necessity for some improvements being made 'to the dock at Petewawa, and an item was put in last year's estimates to provide for that work. I regret to say that the appropriation has disappeared from the estimates this year, and I cannot too strongly urge on the Minister of Public Works the great necessity for these improvements. At a meeting of the Pembroke Navigation Company held recently, and at which I was present, the directors of that company asked me to bring to the attention of the government the present state of that dock. The minister knows that when that dock was constructed a few years ago, there was some defect in the plans and at low water it is almost impossible to get to the dock, there being a reef at one side which is very dangerous to navigation. Although there was an item in the estimates last year no work was done on the dock. We are not particular as to whether the government will improve the existing Mr. EDWARDS.
dock or build a new one in front of the military camp. Petewawa, since the establishment of the military camp there, has become a very important place, and it is absolutely necessary that some means should be provided to reach it by water. I would strongly impress on the minister the advisability of taking this matter into consideration and putting an item in the estimates for this work.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
I will give it consideration.
Lake Nipissing-improvement of navigation through Narrows between upper and lower reaches of West bay and up to Monetteville, $2,000.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: What is this item for?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: The obiect of this is to give communication between the upper and lower reaches of West bay to Monetteville, which is quite a new settlement, but a very important one. There are a large number of farmers in there who produce a good deal of produce, chiefly hay. By doing this work, which will not cost more than $6,300, it will give them eighteen or twenty miles of navigation and enable them to get their produce to market at less expense than if they had to haul it by road. A delegation of farmers from that district waited on me some time ago and made out such an exceedingly strong case that I thought an appropriation should be provided.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Is it not a fact that $5,000 has been already expended on this work and that its object simply is to provide a small canal to .connect a small inland lake with Monetteville and Lake Nipissing?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: The hon. gentleman is nearly right; $4,800 has been expended and this is to pay for the work. The work had to be done this winter if it is to be of use next summer.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I call the attention of the House to the fact that this is a small inland lake three miles in extent, and that it has no connection, or very little connection with Lake Nipissing except during high water. The fact is that a man friendly to the government erected a small sawmill with a capacity of 8,000 or 10,000 feet a day at the wrong end of the lake and unfortunately for him and he had to scow his lumber to the end of the lake so as to get dt across to Lake Nipissing. In order to facilitate him in getting out his lumber the government undertook this work, which I am informed was commenced shortly before the election and carried on for a short time. It will be of no use to anybody except to the man who owns the sawmill. This is a long way from Monetteville and I hardly think there is any danger of it ever getting to that village.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: My hon. friend certainly is misinformed. My information is that there is a population of over 1,000 within the settlement that will be to a very considerable extent benefited by this improvement. It will give navigation for about 18 miles. The three gentlemen who waited on me did not come before the election. Mr. Monet was one of the gentlemen but I do not remember the others. So interested were they that they came all the way to Ottawa to urge this work. They made out a very strong case indeed. They showed there was a very large settlement in there, that vast quantities of hay were raised in that vicinity and that this would give navigation of about 15 miles. Mr. Corriveau the engineer of my department in charge of work in that locality confirmed their statement as to the necessity for this work.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Is this work under contract or not, and was it commenced before the election ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Almost everything dates from the election. It is like the burning of Rome, the great fire in St. John and many other things that aTe important. My hon. friend has the date of the election as the one burning subject which he thinks of by day and dreams of by night. There was a report on October 8, 1908, from Mr. Corriveau making a recommendation as to opening this channel 275 feet long and 30 feet wide and also doing some rock cutting, and the work was authorized. There was an appropriation of $3,000 for it made at the last session of parliament and it was quite proper that the work should be gone on with.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: When was the work started ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
In October. Then the delegation I referred to came down after the election. The work had been gone on with as far as the appropriation allowed and the deputation said to me that it was very important to finish the work this winter. A gentleman named Levesque who is doing quite a laTge business up there said that if these men were permitted to finish the work under the direction of the engineer he would pay the men and if parliament made the appropriation well and good, he would take the risk of that. That shows how anxious they were to have the work done. I said:	* If you do so I shall
bring the matter before my colleagues and if they agree I will put a sum in the estimates to complete the work.' That is why we are asking this additional amount.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I understand that this channel, in place of opening 15 miles of navigation, will open three miles; the lake is three or four miles long.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: No, about 15 miles long.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: The lake is about three miles long and they would have to go around it three or four times to measure 15 miles.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
Oh, no. There is a short distance that has to be dredged and it is 15 miles from there to the head of
navigation.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: People acquainted with the country say not, and that there will be only two or three months in the year during which you will have water to get into the ditch.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I believe Mr. Monet is an intelligent man, a man of high reputation and he said it would be about 15 miles of navigation.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: What is the length of the lake ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: About three miles.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: How far is it from the channel to the head of the lake?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: The channel is between Lake Nipissing and the small lake.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: What is the distance between Lake Nipissing and Shanty lake?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Some few hundred yards only.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I am sure the hon. gentleman is mistaken.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: That happens to be in the district that I have the honour to represent and I think that perhaps I would not be doing my duty if I did not say that, although I have not actually been over the ground, if Mr. Monet and the other people from that locality gave that information to the minister they were abusing his confidence. I have been in past there and while I do not actually know whether the lake is three or four miles long, I think I am safe in saying it is not more than four, and I think this has been a case I am sorry to say, of misplaced confidence. I am sorry to have to say it, because I like to see improvements going on in my own district where they are needed.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Does the hon. gentleman disapprove of this expenditure?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Yes, yes.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Wait a moment and allow the hon. member to answer.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: You cannot undo it now because the money is spent.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
I will tell you. A gentleman named McKee had a small mill at that lake as the hon. member (Mr. Arthurs) has said. He built the mill in the wrong place, at the head of this little lake

and he found he had to place his lumber upon scows, bring them down to the little portage, draw the lumber over the portage and then put it on boats again to bring it to Sturgeon Falls. Just when the election was approaching, men were set to work to do a little digging in anticipation, I suppose, of having to handle a good deal of lumber over there this year, but unfortunately the little mill has not been running this year, not a log has been taken out, so there will be no lumber to be transported there. There are a few farmers there but not a great many. They have misinformed the minister when they say there are 1,000 people, there is nothing like that at all. It will be a little benefit to these people because small craft can go in and out and it will help them to bring out a little hay, but at the same time there is a road parallel to this and for my part I would much prefer seeing that expenditure made in several other places I might point out where it is more required, as at Latchford or New Liskeard. If you investigate this I think you will find I have represented the case to you exactly as it is.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Does it open up 15 miles of navigation?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: No.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Would this be possible? I was told certainly it would save fifteen miles of haul over the road for the farmers' produce. What does the hon. gentleman say with regard to the distance saved as compared with the water route?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: About four miles.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Fifteen was stated to me and I will make inquiries.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Are we to understand that the minister told the deputation to go home and spend the money and he would see that it would be returned?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I think we will let this item stand.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Has the money been expended?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Under this assurance.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Are we to understand that the minister told the deputation to spend the money and he would recommend a repayment by the government?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: What took place was this. They were very anxious that the matter should be proceeded with.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: That was during the election.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
No, it was after the election. There was a gentleman with the deputation, who was a man of considerable Mr. GEO. GORDON.
means, and he said the matter was so important he would advance the money to these people. I said that I did not know whether parliament would vote it or not.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: How much?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
We are asking $2,000. I have put in the item upon the representation that the work would open up this extent of navigation which I stated. If I have been deceived, I would not ask the committee to pass the item.
- Mr. GEO. TAYLOR. The hon. minister should pay it out of his own pocket if he has put this in on false representations.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I would sooner do that than ask parliament to vote it, after what the hon. member for Nipissing has said.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Did the hon. minister allow these gentlemen to go on and spend the money and then put an item in the estimates for parliament to vote, without sending an engineer there?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: There was an engineer there.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Did he get a report from an engineer on which he based this estimate?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: An engineer made a report, Mr. Corriveau. He is not here now. But upon the statement made by the hon. member from Nipissing (Mr. Gordon) I will allow the item to stand.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I understood the minister to say that the engineer stated it would give fifteen miles navigation?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: No, these gentlemen said that.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: What was the gentleman's name who offered to disburse this large amount himself?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Mr. Levesque.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: There has been some $2,300 spent on this, and I hope that the government will go on with the work and finish it as otherwise that money would be absolutely lost. I stated awhile ago that this would be of some little use to those few farmers, but the statement made by those men who came here that there would be a saving of fifteen miles was not correct. I do not think there would be that saving. It would be absolutely wrong to spend the money if the work had not been begun, but now that part of it is done we ought to complete it.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Upon that admission, we had better carry the item.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
I am informed there is a bridge down near Cardinal for which the Minister of Railways has no particular

use. It has been lying there for four or five years. Would he take into his serious consideration the sending of that bridge down to Wolfe Island and putting it across the canal?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: The council of Edwards-burg want to buy it.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
Have you placed a
price on it?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I am not sure.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
I suppose you will
consider an offer from Wolfe Island?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: We will be glad to get the most we can for it.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: The township of Ed-wardsburg do not require the bridge, they have built another one.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: This discussion must be out of order when we are considering Public Works estimates.

speakerposition: Deputy Speaker and Chair of Committees of the Whole of the House of Commons
maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
I hope hon. gentlemen will not too long keep away from the item under consideration.
Meaford-harbour improvements, $400.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: What is this item for?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: This will complete. The contract was for $34,742.87. Then there was dredging in addition. The total expenditure to 15th February was $44,086.64, and the appropriation for the same year was $43,700, leaving $386.64 due.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Has there been any plan adopted for the improvement of this harbour-any definite permanent plan?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Yes, but I do not know whether I can say that it is unalterable, like the laws of the Medes and Persians. There was a good deal of discussion as to the best plan, and we adopted one on which we are proceeding. I have here the particulars of the work done during the past year. The contract was, first for an extension 50 feet in an easterly direction at the inner end of the breakwater, which was then 430 feet long and 30 feet wide, with a view of affording additional protection from the northerly gales to vessels lying loading at the elevators in the harbour and those wintering there. Then to build a revetment wall of pile work and concrete, 300 feet in length. Also put down close sheet piling 135 feet in length and dredging to 30 feet below the low water level.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: We had a severe storm there last fall, and it was a great disappointment to the people to find that after spending all that money, tne harbour was still in such a state that the boats were torn from their moorings and a number driven against the bridge and their upper works destroyed, and quite a number had to be brought to Owen Sound to make them reasonably safe for the winter. My object is not to criticise but to see if 1 cannot impress on the minister the advisability of changing the plan he has adopted. When, after spending $43,000, we find that the harbour does not afford sufficient protection to vessels, some change should be made. That is why the other day I impressed on the hon. minister the advisability of putting something in the supplemen-taries. Unless something be done now, there will be further injuries this year. This is a case which would justify the minister in placing in the estimates an amount for the purpose of remedying as far as possible the defects proven to exist in that harbour. Meaford is one of the harbours on the south shore of Georgian bay, which it is the policy of the hon. gentleman to deepen and improve, for the accommodation of large vessels unloading grain, and I would urge on him to do something this year to preserve the work already done.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I shall be very glad to have the matter looked into in view of what my hon. friend has said. He speaks of putting an amount in the supplementaries, but I have not yet been advised by the Minister of Finance that we are going to have any, so that I am unable to say whether or not it will be possible to make any provision this year.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: The hon. gentleman (Mr. Pugsley) got a memorial sent to him by the town of Meaford?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Does he remember what it recited?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: No, but it will be looked into very carefully.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: When does the minister expect to begin building the wharf at Brighton village? I hope that soon he will be asking for tenders.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: No.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Did not the minister promise a wharf last election?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I do not think so.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: That was the understanding in the riding.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Did the hon. gentleman (Mr. Owen) convey that message to the electors?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: No, not I. It came from Ottawa headquarters, and the minister did not send it through me. Somebody else delivered it.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I will have to make inquiries.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: There was a post office promised for Campbellford, too. It was promised right from the platform on nomination day.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I am glad the hon. gentleman has mentioned Campbellford, for it gives me an opportunity to say that I have seen a letter from the gentleman to whom he refers, and that gentleman denies, in the most positive terms, that he made any promise of a public building for the town of Campbellford.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: When did he deny that?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: In a letter I have seen.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I never said he made the promise.	[DOT]

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: The statement was made in this House.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Not by me. What is the name of the gentleman charged with making that promise?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Some hon. member of the House made the charge. I will look up the letter from the gentleman who wa.s the candidate.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I did not say that the candidate made the promise.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: If my memory serves me right, some hon. member of the House made that statement.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I am more convinced than ever now that the promise was made from Ottawa.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Will the minister bring down the report of the engineer with reference to the item of $2,000 for Lake Nipissing before concurrence takes place?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
I shall be very glad to.
Owen Sound harbour-dredging and pile protection work, $15,700.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Who has the contract? Is this money to finish the work?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: This money has been expended, or will be before the close of the fiscal year.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Who has the contract, and how is the work being done?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Bowman, Southampton.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: What was the total contract?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: This is dredge work, and is paid for by the yard, $2.75 for rock and 25 cents for other material.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: How much rock has he excavated?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: No rock.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Was this let by tender?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Yes, Mr. Bowman was the lowest tenderer.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Who were the tenderers?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I have not that information before me. I think it has all been submitted to the House and will be found in the returns or in 'Hansard' of last session.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I was not here and I would like to have that information.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I will be glad to get it for my hon. friend (Mr. Middlebro).

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Were there disputes between the contractors and the department as to the work done in the harbour?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: There was some slight dispute as to the work done in a dredging slip. The matter was not brought to my attention. There was some question as to whether the contractor was to be paid for certain work.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Can the minister give a statement as to the amount in dispute? Was there any dispute as to the work on the revetment?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I will find out.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: What amount has been expended on the harbour of Owen Sound to date?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I think $453,000, since 1874.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Who is the inspector who certifies to the quantity of earth removed ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I could not say, but I will get that information also.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I will postpone further discussion until we have the facts. I suppose the item stands ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I hope the hon. gentleman (Mr. Middlebro) will not ask to have the item stand. These are our supplementary estimates for the current year and these votes are to close up business. When we come for the full amount in the estimates of 1909-1910, the matter can be discussed. Will this be satisfactory?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Yes, especially as the money is expended.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.

Silver Centre-wharf on west side of Lake Temiskaming-further amount, $500.

Southampton-extension of and repairs to town dock, $16,000.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Is there any work being done to deepen the eastern entrance?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: What is the intention of the government with regard to it?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: There is no present intention one way or the other. My information is that there is sufficient water now for the purpose of navigation, and it does not seem to be necessary to do any more dredging at the eastern entrance at present.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Is there any appropriation for that? That entrance fills up every season, every season it becomes almost blocked, and requires dredging in order to make it navigable in the spring.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: There is no special appropriation for that. We took one vote for it, improvements at Toronto harbour, quite a large vote. But with regard to the eastern entrance, I may say that until quite recently the dredging has never been properly done. We think we have now done it thoroughly we have deepened it to give sufficient depth! and we do not expect it will fill in in the very near future.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: What appropriation has the minister made for the protection of the island breakwater?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: What is the policy of the minister for the coming year as to these estimates which are now being voted for dredging in different places in Ontario and Quebec? maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I have not quite decided yet. Last year I was over-persuaded to call for new tenders and it cost the country about $200,000. I do not want to repeat that. If my chief engineer reports that the work of last season has been satisfactorily performed and that the prices are fair and reasonable and I am satisfied of it I would be rather inclined to continue the contracts for the work which is necessary during the coming year.

Toronto, Aug. 28, 1908.
J. S. Davis, Esq.,
Barrister, &c.,

I am instructed by the Temiskaming and Northern Ontario Commission to notify you that on account of your failure to construct building, as required by your agreement of day of	for purchase by you
of lots	in townsite of Latchford,
said agreement is liable to cancellation, and unless you take steps forthwith to comply with the agreement we shall cancel same and refund to you the amount that has been paid for said lots. We register this letter and require your acknowledgement on or before the 10th day of June, 1908.
They have notified these people that unless they build forthwith their claims will be cancelled and they will refund them the money. That would place an exact pi ice on the value of these lots.
We have refunded purchase price to

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
I hope the minister will pardon me for being so persistent, but I do not think he realizes that there are thousands of people at the head of the Montreal river who will be unable to get

in a sufficient quantity of supplies to carry them over the summer if this work is not done, and may therefore be exposed to great suffering. Mr. Englehart has assured me he will do everything in his power to have this trifling question about the land adiusted. and I "hope the minister will go on with the work.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
The commissioners own this land and if they choose to put an exorbitant price on the lots it is their own
business.	.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: There are only ten lots owned by the Ontario government.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: They asked us to pay $160 each for lots which during the boom at Latchford they were unable to sell, while they sold lots far superior to these at an unset nrice of $70 or $80 each. It is not that the $1,600 is so veTy large but if we pay $160 each for the very worst lots on the town site it would mean that this government would be mulcted in very heavy damages if we had to pay a relatively high price to the private owners of better lots. What I complain of is, that when this government proposes to do a thing for the benefit of that section of the country, and for the benefit of the people there, and for developing property which is owned by the Ontario government, and out of which the Ontario government will get large sums for royalties, they should hold us up for the very last dollar and even double the value of these lots on us. I do not propose to engage upon the construction of this dam unless I can see where we stand with regard to the land damages. If we are going to me mulcted in thousands of dollars of damages for flooding lands I must stay my hand and not proceed with this work. Mr. Englehart in this letter says that if there is any way in which he can be of assistance to expedite the matter he would only be too happy, and I can tell my hon. friend (Mr. Gordon) that if he wants to be of assistance he can get the Ontario government to give us a quit claim deed of the land. If that were done, I can assure my hon. friend that it would go a long way to' help us forward towards the construction of this very necessary public work.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: At the time of the sale at Latchford there were no buildings erected, but now it is quite a little town and the lots are more valuable than they were then.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: But they have not been able to sell them.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
They have been treating with the government here and they would not want to sell them to any one else in the meantime. I would ask the Minister of Public Works to consider that the Ontario government has built that railway without one cent of subsidy being re-Mr. GEO. GORDON.
ceived from the Dominion government, and I think it is the only Tailway in Canada which stands in that position.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: And they say it is paying very handsome returns.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I think it is doing very well, but at the same time the majority of the people of Ontario hold that the Dominion government owes to the people of Ontario $6,400 per mile for every mile of that Tailroad. In view of that, and of the great urgency of this undertaking, I hope the Minister of Public Works will not let a few paltry dollars stand in the way, particularly when the money will go into the hands of people who will take good care of it.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: It is nut'a question of the amount of money we might pay for these lots, but if we pay $160 for each of these worthless lots for which they have been unable to obtain purchasers it will become the basis for the claims of private owners who have much better lots. I can tell my hon. friend (Mr. Gordon) that if the Ontario government will cut the amount m two I will close with them to-morrow.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: On these ten lots ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Yes, and then they can give us a quit claim deed on the other lots and let us deal with the purchasers.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: That is, if they give you these ten lots for $80 each ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Yes, and then let them convey to us the other lots upon which other people have claims and upon which they apparently have no claim except the right to receive some purchase money.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Yes, so that we will be able to deal with the purchasers and take up the whole thing and bring it to a head and get it settled and go on with the work at once.

^ Mr. W. R. SMYTH. Why is there $12,700 in the supplementaries? The appropriation was $6,000. You have exceeded that by $12,700. When was the work ' commenced and was it done by contract?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: It was done by contract let on September 5, 1905. We were pressed very strongly to do this work at the mouth of the Spanish river, in fact we had been pressed for it for some time. The outlay during the year just closing was for the removal of 66,738 cubic yards of quicksand and clay sand by the dredge 'Meade' from September 21 to November 14, from two long sand bars, 6,000 yards up stream from the mouth of the Spanish river to secure a depth of 12 feet at low water. The expenditure for that was $16,708. In addition there was material and labour for the building of a pile and concrete pier at Massey 15 miles above the mouth of the river, which cost $1,861.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Who had the contract for the dredging and was it let by tender?

speechtext: The C. S. Boone Dredging & Construction Company of Toronto. The contract was let on September 5, and the price was 25 cents per cubic yard.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: What was the necessity for the work and why was it so urgent?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: There is a company there called, I think, the Spanish River Navigation Company. They are navigating the Spanish river and they urged this work very strongly. The hon. gentleman who formerly represented the constituency also urged it. We had very strong requests for this work.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: The minister perhaps is aware that an appropriation has been made for this work several times. As far back as 10 or 12 years ago there was an appropriation of $10,000 in the estimates for this particular work. That did beautifully during the election of that year. Then it was dropped out of sight. Four years afterwards, an item appears in large type in the local newspapers favourable to my late opponent stating that the government had revoted $10,000 for the Spanish river improvements. That was lost sight of immediately after the elections. This last time there was $6,000 of an appropriation for this work.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: The hon. gentleman sees I did not lose sight of it.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
It became very urgent indeed last fall that this work should be done for reasons of which the hon. minister is no doubt aware. Why was
$12,700 more than the appropriation for this work expended? Was it not as necessary ten, eight, six or four years ago as it was last fall? Why the urgency for doing- the work at the particular period at which it was done?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: That is a very proper question.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
