speechtext: And a question I am afraid the minister would have a hard time answering to the satisfaction of the people of the district of Algoma.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: You just try me now.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I know he is an expert, but notwithstanding all that the people of the district of Algoma know full well why the work was done when it was done, and during a period of the year when dredges are usually being laid up in winter quarters.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Does not my hon. friend think the expenditure was absolutely necessary in the interests of navigation?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: If it was really necessary, it was necessary 10 or 8 years ago.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Is it necessary?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: It is no more necessary now than it was then.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Was it not necessary last fall?	[DOT]

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: It was done purely and simply for political purposes' " '

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I am interested to hear my hon. friend say that.	*

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I am never afraid to tell the truth.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I am sure my hon. friend would not be, because I have great respect for him.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: And I have great respect for my word.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I cannot see how, if the dredging was necessary and it has now been done and some 66,000 cubic yards removed from these two large sand bars, the expense has been wasted. This dredging is to give a depth of 12 feet.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Does it give it?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: You have to dredge out from time to time to keep down to the 12 feet. We have now taken out 66,000 cubic yards, but if it is not deep enough we will have to dredge deeper.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Has the minister anything in the main estimates for the continuation of that work?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
Not that I am aware
of.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: The work the minister has done is absolutely wasted unless he continues to dredge the river much further up than he has done.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: That is a different thing. What my hon. friend means now is that we must go further and spend more money.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: If it is necessary to do it at all it is necessary to do it right.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: With regard to the work not being done some years ago my hon. friend is quite Tight in calling attention to it; the difficulty was to get a dredge. It happened that last fall it was possible to get a dredge. The dredge of the C. S. Boone Company had got through with its work on the Blind river, and we were able to have it moved down to do this work at the mouth of the Spanish river.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: That dredge almost got there by lightning.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Of course, because it got through with the other work and the sooner it would get to work on the Spanish river the sooner the owners would make some money, but in the busy spring or summer this yeaT it might have been impossible to get a dredge there as has happened in other years. I may say frankly that Mr. Dyment found a great deal of fault with me and my department because we had not put the dredge to work before. I explained that there was no dredge available, but just as soon as this dredge was available she was put to work on the Spanish river. We have done the amount of dredging I have mentioned, and if it is necessary to go to a greater depth I would hope that before very long we would be able to continue the work so as to effect what I think my hon. friend would say is a very much needed public improvement.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: It may be needed, but the money expended was simply thrown away, in the way the wont was done and during the season in which it was done.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I cannot see that. It was done at so much a cubic yard.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
Yes, but the same number of cubic yards is in that same channel today. You cannot take a boat through the channel you dredged last fall. I am doubtful if the money was spent which we are asked to vote. 'The dredge was there only a very short time. During the election campaign, my opponent made the boast on the public platform that he had ordered the department to send that dredge to the mouth of the Spanish river, and that it would be there in a few days and sure enough it was. But it took ten years to get that dredge there, according to the minister, because there was an appropriation made ten years ago for that purpose
and also four years ago. Yet he now says that the work was so urgent last fall, the dredge had to be sent there during the election. But if the work was so urgent last fall, why is there not this year a sum in the estimates to complete it and make that channel navigable for the coming summer? If the work is to be of any benefit and if the boats are to be enabled to reach that dock which the government built up the Spanish river some twelve or fourteen miles, the minister will have to do a good deal more dredging. They built the dock before there was water enough for a boat to get there.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: My hon. friend is mistaken. The vessels of the Spanish River Navigation Company weie running up to the place where this dock was built. I recognize that it may be desirable to do further dredging. My hon. friend has asked why there is not an amount in the main estimates for this purpose.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Because there is no election.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: No, but it is in accordance with the policy of economy which we have been obliged to adopt.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: There is no economy when you spent $12,700 more than was appropriated last year.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: That is done and my hon. friend is asking about next year. I cannot say whether we shall be able to do further dredging next year or not. I shall have to give the matter further consideration.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Is the hon. minister aware that the dredge in question employed 23 American citizens doing the work?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I was not aware of that.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I am informed on reliable authority that there were 23 American citizens on the dredge at the mouth of the Spanish river doing that work.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: How much was in the estimates last year for harbours and rivers in Ontario and how much this year?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I have not got the main estimates here. The hon. gentleman will find the amount in those estimates.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I want to see how far the policy of economy is applied to Ontario in respect of these items.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: It is applied to Ontario to no greater extent than to any other province in Canada.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: The estimates were $1,619,780 last year and $795,250 this year.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: When did that dredge stop doing work on the Spanish river ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: On the 14th of November.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: When did it begin ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: The contract was let the 5th of September and it began the 21st.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Was there anything in the estimates last year for that work ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: What was the price paid?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Twenty-five cents per cubic yard, scow measurement.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I would like to ask the hon. minister if he proposes to do any dredging at Port Credit this year. For several years his predecessors promised that a certain amount of dredging would be done there. The excuse always given for not doing it was that no dredge was available, hut that excuse can hardly be advanced now since the appropriations are somewhat smaller for Ontario than in former years, and consequently the dredges will not be so busy. There is always some work going on at Hamilton and Toronto, and Port Credit harbour lies between the two and is very close to either of them. In the appropriation we have this year, may we expect the government to carry out the promise that some work would be done at this important point?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I am not aware of any promise by my predecessors and none was certainly made by me. I am not in a position to say whether any dredging will be done there the coming season or not. We have no sum in the estimates for it, and I do not see how it is possible for me to do all the absolutely urgent work the coming year out of the general dredging vote. With regard to Port Credit, there is another difficulty, and that is that it is owned by a company. Many years ago, before confederation, the Ontario government was in the habit of handing over certain harbours to private corporations, and Port Credit unfortunately is in that position. I do not know if that would be an effectual bar to our dredging there, but the most I can say is that I will think the matter over, but I cannot hold out any strong hope.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
My hon. friend has never expended any money at that point but there was some expended there some years ago. My hon. friend has not given any promise, but two of his predecessors gave promises on the floor of the House which I quoted in a discussion two years ago. If my hon. friend will look over the history of his department, he will find that two of his predecesors promised they would spend some money at that important point. I never could understand why they did not do it. My hon. friend is very careful of 105
course in not promising, but I hope he will look into the matter and see that some money is expended there. It is a very important centre and should be kept open in the public interest. There _ is a good deal of traffic on Lake Ontario between Hamilton and Toronto. Indeed, it is a harbour of refuge in many times of storm. I think the minister should send his engineer to examine and should give this matter rather serious consideration. I may expect that from the minister, I suppose, this year ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I will make a note of it and think it over.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: The minister can hardly give as a reason for not spending money on the Port Credit harbour the fact that it is owned by a private corporation, because the Dominion has expended money on harbours similarly owned.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Where?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: In Nova Scotia, Glace bay-I think that is the harbour-is owned by a coal company, and the Dominion has spent a great deal of money there; it practically made the harbour.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I think the hon. gentleman is mistaken. There is no parallel in Canada with this harbour of Port Credit. I am sure Glace bay is not a parallel. The foreshore may be owned, but not the harbour, not the water.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I do not insist on the name, but certainly one of these harbours is owned by the coal company.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Does the minister say that the government does not spend money on [DOT]harbours owned by private parties in any part of Canada?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I do not say that, because I think there has been some such expenditure, but I say it creates a difficulty, as, I am sure, the hon. gentleman will recognize.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
As the minister has expended $18,000 on the Spanish river, I would urge upon him the necessity of continuing the work. For two reasons: the first is ftiat the work has been done improperly, I say advisedly, but with all due respect to the engineers and those who did the work. There is a great deal of shifting sand, and I do not think it was dredged wide enough to prevent the sand going back into the same ground. That is one reason-the minister ought to try to save the work that has been done by doing more. Another is that, as' he is dredging at one end of the river and has a dock at the other with no means of getting to his dock with any satisfaction with any steamboat of any size, he might better continue improving the river all the way between



the dock and where the improvements have been already made. No doubt, he is aware that there is a good deal of conten-the lumbermen. Money could well be spent tion between the steamboat company and by assisting both the lumbermen and steamboat company in connection with the chan-uel. But as the minister was so anxious to spend the money last fall, and spend it lavishly, I hope he will find reason to continue the work this year and save the work already done. We will see what can be done.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Has the minister given Port Bruce any more thought?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I have been thinking Port Bruce over.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: May I ask if the minister has been thinking favourably of it?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Well, I hear very good reports of Port Bruce.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: The minister would not like to make me a promise to-night?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Not to-night.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I do not want very much.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: The hon. gentleman is modest, I know; and I really will think it over. But I would sooner give the hon. gentleman the dredging than give him the promise.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I desire to draw attention to the condition of affairs with regard to minor wharfs that are being built on inland waters. I find that an agent is being appointed by the government in some instances and in others not. In these latter cases, apparently nobody is in charge of the wharf after it is built. Instances come to my mind of wharfs being simply appropriated, sometimes to the detriment of the public. But, if an accident happens, a plank gets out of place, there is nobody to look after it. I made inquiry, last year and was told that the wharfs where I live were under control of an engineer at Toronto, 145 miles away. How are these matters managed after the wharfs are built?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
The proper, the regular course, would be to transfer the wharf to the Department of Marine and Fisfieries. The Minister of Marine and Fisheries appoints a wharfinger and gives him a percentage of the wharfage tolls received. In that way, there is somebody to take care of the wliarf and see to it that the necessary repairs are made. But sometimes, as the collection of tolls would be quite burdensome, especially to the farmers who are using the wharf in a small way, my department has been asked not to make the transfer to the Marine and Fisheries Department. In the majority of cases, I am sorry to say, both under the old government Mr. SMYTH.
and under this government, that request has been acceded to, and the transfer has not been made, no wharfinger has been appointed and no tolls collected. An arrangement may be made with a steamship company so that they may use the wharf, but that is unsatisfactory. I recognize the importance of the question that the hon. gentleman (Mr. Wright) raises. The Minister of Marine and_ Fisheries has been considering the question how to deal with these small wharfs, and he thought it might not be inadvisable to lease them, to the steamboat companies, or charge them so much for the right to come to the wharf, or, perhaps, to lease the wharf to the municipal council and so do away with the necessity of charging a farmer a toll for getting a barrel of flour or ten pounds of sugar delivered on the wharf. That is a very obnoxious tax to impose upon the people, and we are endeavouring to do away with it.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: While the) minister seems to be in a generous mood in granting wharfs and harbour improvements, I would like to ask if his attention has been called to the necessity of a landing pier at St. Williams, in the county of Nonfolk, on the north shore of Lake Erie. Would he say whether he has received an application, or some representation as to the necessity of such a work?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: My attention has not been called to St. Williams, or to the. necessity of a wharf there. If I were to accede to all the requests made from the other side my estimates would roll up tremendously.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Work was commenced last year to rebuild a wharf at the village of Lakefield. The work is not yet completed, and I think the department has been requested to increase the appropriation by a few thousand dollars, in order to extend that work properly. It is a . good time now to do this, seeing that the work is still incomplete. Is it the intention of the government to grant further aid?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
The hon. gentleman who represents West Peterboro (Mr. Stratton) has brought that matter forcibly to my attention. Although my department obtained the appropriation for the money, we transferred the work to the Department of Railways, and it is being done under that department. The question of providing for an extension during the coming year is now under consideration.
Manitoba-River Assiniboine-improvements near Portage la Prairie, $250.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
I desire this item to stand until the return which I moved for on the 17th of February, is brought down. The minister knows that I called his attention to it before the orders of the day

were called this afternoon, and told him that this Teturn had not been brought down. It is in reference to this particular piece of work, and we wish to get some facts before we can intelligently dispose of this item.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I want to appeal to the good judgment of my hon. friend and ask him not to press that request, for the reason that these are the supplementary estimates for the current year, and it is important that they should be got through so as to close up the accounts before the 31st of March. But I will say to my hon. friend that the return will be brought down right away, and when we are considering the main estimates he shall have an opportunity of discussing it.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: That is the reason why I do not want this item to go through, because the information I am seeking is in reference to the current year.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: My hon. friend can discuss that on the main estimates.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I do not see why this item should go through to-night; we have another week before us to the end -of the month.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: When we come to the main estimates my hon. friend will have the same opportunity of discussing it-I will undertake that-as if we were to discuss it to-night.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I think the main estimates for Manitoba have gone through. Perhaps the minister will bring down the information before concurrence.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Yes, I will do that.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: There has been an arrangement made between the hon. member for North Toronto (Mr. Foster) and the Minister of Finance that these supplement-aries shall be disposed of before the end of the month.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Possibly the information we get in these returns will be such that we shall want to strike out the item.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I will make another suggestioon to my hon. friend for Macdonald (Mr. Staples). If he will be good enough to call over to the office of the deputy minister to-morrow morning, we will show him all the papers, and then this can be discussed on concurrence.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
I would be glad to accede to the hon. gentleman's wishes, but I am not the only member from the province of Manitoba. The member for Portage la Prairie (Mr. Meighen) has been following this matter up as well as myself. I would like a little time to investigate. There has been a large expenditure 1051
there, a very foolish expenditure, in my opinion, which was made for the purpose of securing votes at that particular time. There are many things in connection with that expenditure that we want to unearth and bring to light; then we will be in a position to take up this item intelligently.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I will have my messenger bring the papers here to-morrow to the hon. gentleman.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Can we have an opportunity of discussing this to-morrow?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: On concurrence.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I have had some experience in the last four years, and I know how difficult it is to discuss an item_ on concurrence. Not much attention is paid to items of this nature on concurrence.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Yes, there will be.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I do not think I am asking too much. It is very necessary that the work which has been done there should be completed. Take it also further down the Assinaboine river; there was public money expended on lot 160 and, according to the advice that I have had from the council of St. Franqois Xavier, a large part of this country is going to be flooded if the werk is going to be left in the condition in which it is to-day. I could go to the office and look over the papers, but my hon. _ friend from Portage La Prairie (Mr. Meighen), who is not here to-night, wants to get this information also, as well as other members from that province.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: The work for which this item is asked is to close up the balance due on the channel at Portage La Prairie for the purpose of relieving the flooding, and we do intend to do some more work next year with respect to _ these improvements which we believe will have the effect of preventing the flooding of the country. We are approaching very closely to the 31st March; it is desirable to have the supplementaries through and it is understood that this can be discussed upon concurrence. If my hon. friend will telephone my deputy where he will be in the morning, I will have a clerk in my office bring over all the papers and show them to my hon. friend, and to any other hon. gentlemen from Manitoba who desire to see them, and I can assure my hon. friend that he will have the fullest opportunity of discussing this matter upon concurrence. I should think that would be very much better, if he wishes to get his views before his constituents, than to discuss the question tonight. Let us get through with the items.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
On that understanding we can let the item go. I will take the op
0.3.35

portunity of bringing it up some day upon the orders of the day.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Quite right; that is a good idea.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I have a -letter from a councillor who represents a ward in the municipality of St. Francois Xavier and he tells me that certain work that has been done by this government on lot 160 has been left in such a condition that unless steps are taken to secure it in some way the country will be flooded.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: What description of work is that?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I believe the banks are subsiding and that it is necessary to do some piling. The information I get from there is that the government promised to do the piling last fall. It has not been done. I am not clear as to what the nature of the work is, I must confess, and I would like to get some information as to that myself.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: That would have nothing to do with this item.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
No, it is further down the river. Now that we are on the supply estimates, I consider that I am quite in order in asking if it is the intention of the government to do anything at St. Laurent? Four years ago there was great activity at that place. A dredge was bought a few days before the election, it was put to work, a number of men were employed, and it was said that they were going to build a wharf for the convenience of the people of that particular constituency of Macdonald. But, on the day following the election the dredge was taken away and we have not heard anything of it since. Last October they promised to bring the dredge back. They were very sorry that they could not get the dredge at that particular time but the assurance was given to the people there that if they would vote for the Liberal candidate there would be no doubt but that this work would be completed. The people of that portion of the municipality of Macdonald accepted the promise of the government candidate to a certain extent, or at least, an adverse majority was given against me there. I hope the Minister will not deceive them but that he will go on and make good the promise which was presented to these people by my opponent. The work is practically useless as it stands. It is about half done, the people cannot get near it, and it is necessary to do certain work down across the lagoon before it is of any value whatever. I hope the minister will take the trouble to inquire into this Mr. STAPLES.
matter and make good the promise presented to the people on the public platform last October.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I will have the matter looked into.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
If I may be permitted to speak on the item I would like to mention a question which affects my own riding. In some way or other I missed the discussion of the public works items dealing with wharfs and bridges in the province of Alberta. I have been informed by the deputy clerk that these items are through although I do not understand how they could have got through without my knowledge. There was in the estimates of the last two years an appropriation of about $8,000 for protecting the banks of the Old Man river at the town of McLeod. I have already spoken to the minister on this subject privately and he gave me a good deal of encouragement to hope that there would probably be an item m the Supply estimates this year, but I am sorry to say that I do not find such an item. I think we have a very strong claim upon the government to undertake and carry out this work and it does seem to me like penalizing the people of that district because they sent a Conservative at the last election. That work was promised at the time by the department here and it was held up before the people of the constituency as one of the works that was going to be carried out. Immediately after the election is over I find that the item is withdrawn. I think we have an'especially strong claim to have a small amount of work done for more reasons than one. I find that the minister is very generous in granting money for works of this description in other parts of the country, but that he has done very little work of this nature in the province of Alberta. I think that in the two provinces of Saskatchewan and Alberta there is only about $52,000 in this, year's estimates, which I think is a very'small amount compared with the appropriations for works in other parts of the country. I think that we have even a stronger claim than that which I have just mentioned and that is that the government own the land, the rivers and streams; in fact, they own things above and under the water. Another reason is that the town of McLeod, that I am asking this appropriation for, in order to protect the banks of the river, occupies what was a government townsite, a townsite that this government made a great deal of money out of in the past. Another is that there is a government building oil the banks of the river which will be one of the first properties to be destroyed in the event of the banks falling away. There is very great danger that the banks might be undermined to such an extent that the government building might fall down. I

would like to know from the minister, if he is not going to have anything in the estimates this year, if he will pledge his word that the estimates for next year will contain a vote for this very necessary work.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: It is quite true that my hon. friend did call to see me and that he pressed upon my attention the necessity of doing this work at Fort McLeod. The fact that it was regarded by the government as being a necessary work would be evidenced by its having been placed in the estimates last year.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: For two years.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: For two years. But I have been obliged to leave it out of the main estimates this year for the reason I have already stated to the committee. We have been obliged to postpone a great many necessary public works. Probably owing to the decline of the revenue I have had occasion to consider very carefully this question among others of protecting the banks of rivers in the various provinces. We have done work of this character to a certain extent in the past when our revenues were more buoyant. On the Fraser river we divided the cost of such work between the British Columbia government and the 'federal government but in my judgment it is work that can hardly be regarded as federal work. It is not for the improvement of navigation; it is for the protection of property of private owners or property of municipalities and is purely local in its character. If we were to do work of this kind in the various provinces I do not know where the claims upon the federal treasury would end. Only the other day my hon. friend from Chicoutimi called my attention to the danger of a landslide on the St. Lawrence river which if it occurred would destroy property and possibly cause loss 'of life and he urged me to take steps to guard against it; last year the Minister of the Interior urged me to do similar work on the North Saskatchewan at Edmonton, but I felt that this was work for the provincial ot municipal authorities. That is the difficulty with regard to this work at Fort Macleod. It is intended to protect the property of the people of that town. The only ground upon which I thought we might interfere was that if the bank slid away the Dominion public building would likely be the first property to be injured and that appealed to the selfish side of the department. If in order to protect government property it is necessary to do work of this character it might possibly be done, but all I can say to my horn friend now is that it will receive careful consideration.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: If this is a work that should not be undertaken by the federal government why was a vote placed in the estimates for it' two years in succession?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: When we begin to get short of money we have to consider these things very carefully.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: It seems to me the elections had more to do with it than anything else.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Oh, no.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
The minister seems to forget that this was formerly a government townsite and although part of the unsold lots have recently been turned over to the town, yet the government made a great deal of money out of the sale of some of those town lots in days gone by.
Dredging vessels, repairs, further amount required, $100,000.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: What will this make the total amount for repairs in the year?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Were these repairs all done in government yards?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Some in government yards and some in private yards all over the country.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: What is the average cost per annum of operating a dredge in Ontario?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: It depends on the size of the dredge, its capacity, its crew, and other considerations. The cost to operate runs from $5,000 to $35,000.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: At Tiffin and other places, privately owned dredges earn from $40,000 to $60,000 per year. If the government can operate a dredge for from S5,000 to $35,000 then you ought to have more government dredges.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: There is a great deal to be said in favour of that. On the other hand the private contractor seems to be able to get more out of their dredges than the government does.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: In money?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: No, in work. They seem to be able to get their men to work more diligently. It has always been so, I am sorry to say, and possibly it may be so in the future. Of course there is interest on the first cost, and repairs, and so on and it is not all profit. I know a number of people who have been in the dredging business and have found it anything but profitable. Some of them have become bankrupt.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I would like to know one.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Go to Montreal and you will find them.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Is it the intention to keep that dredge working?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: If there is work to be done, we will try to keep it there.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: There is work to be done, but there is not much in the estimates for this year.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
The vote is small, but we hope to be able to keep the government dredges working.
Dredging, maritime provinces, $225,000.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Would the minister give the names of the people to whom this money is to be paid?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: The first item is to cover expenditures incurred in operating the department dredging plant in the maritime provinces from November, 1908, until March, 1909, according to the returns received by the chief accountant up to March 10, $72,598.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Why was the estimate $72,000 out?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: The vote was not for as much as the work has cost. Some of the dredges have been kept going later than had been expected; for instance, the 'Fielding' at St. John has been working right up to a few days ago. Very often they are laid up in the fall.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Does the wharfage the 'Fielding' pays come out of this vote?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Certainly.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Why is it that the 'Fielding' is laid up at a private wharf when there is a government wharf available to lay her up at?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I do not know that. There is a government wharf there owned by the Intercolonial Railway which is required for the use of the Intercolonial Railway and I presume the Intercolonial Railway would not allow us to lay up a dredge there as it would interfere with the use of the Intercolonial Railway wharf by vessels coming there in the ordinary course of business.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Was application made for the use of the wharf?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: It never occurred to me to make such a request, as it would interfere with the business of the wharf.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: The minister will find there is nearly always a vacant place .there where the 'Fielding' could lie.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: The railway wharf is built for commercial purposes and it would seriously interfere with its operation to have a dredge lie there permanently.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: There is generally a place on the northern face of the wharf where it could rest. You often see pilot boats there.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: They can move out quickly. Then the Intercolonial Railway would charge wharfage too.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Not so much.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Proceeding with the items, the second is for contract dredging in Nova Scotia, as follows: At Moser river, Beazley Bros., $8,539. At Yarmouth, Dominion Dredging Company, $59,903, and at Mabou, Dominion Dredging Company, $13,183, a total of $73,086. Then in Mahone bay there is a payment to the Poupore Company $31,052, and at McKinnon harbour payment to the same company, $4,095, a total of $35,147. In New Brunswick, at Grassy island, on the St. John river, there is a payment to S. James Gregory, $4,892, and at Gaspereau to the Maritime Dredging Company of $20,269. There is another payment for work at Mira-michi bay to the Poupore Company of $3,549, and at Dalhousie a payment to A. & H. Loggie of $7,061. That makes a total supplementary requirement to be covered by this vote of $225,143.36.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
What was the rate paid to the Maritime Dredging Company at
Gaspereau ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: 90 cents.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Were tenders called by public advertisement ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: What was the Grassy island rate ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I am not quite sure, but I think it was 50 cents.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: To what depth was the dredging done at Gaspereau ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I do not know, the work was not finished there.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: What did the specifications call for ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I have not the particulars here, that would be given in connection with the main estimates. It is a very exposed and difficult place to dredge, it is up at Port Elgin.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Can the minister state what tenders were received in addition to that of the Maritime Dredging Company ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Only the one tender.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: What was the depth of the Gaspereau river dredging and what length of arm would the dredge require ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I cannot tell that tonight. It was to give accommodation to quite large steamers that go there to carry away lumber.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Is there much rise and fall of the tide ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: There is some tide and it is a very exposed place for dredging. In fact I think they lost one scow right at the beginning.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: How far have the scows to go out ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Out to deep water of course. I have not the exact distance.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Has the Maritime Dredging Company been fully paid for the dredging at Indian Point ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Yes they have been fully paid there.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
In answer to a question which I asked the other day the minister said that the contract for dredging there was let to the Maritime Dredging Company at 50 cents, that the dredging was to be to a depth of 7 feet, and that before dredging the depth of water at that point was about three feet. What does the minister think about that as a price for dredging in such water ? The other night it was stated that the department was having dredging done,
I think at Port Arthur to a depth of 22 feet for 9 cents. It has been a matter of considerable comment, in New Brunswick that the Maritime Dredging Company, in which the minister's friend John E. Moore is the moving spirit, has been able to get a contract at this point for 7 foot dredging at 50 cents a cubic yard, the same price as was paid to Mayes under his contract for dredging to a depth of 32 feet in the harbour of St. John at low water, and 41 cents more per yard than the department has been paying for dredging at Fort William to a depth of 22 feet. I do not know what the minister may think, but it must impress hon. members as a most extraordinary price to pay for the dredging in the St. John river, the easiest kind of dredging, to a depth of seven feet, where the depth before dredging was but three feet. I would like to know what was the purpose of this dredging.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
My hon. friend says that this was the subject of a good deal of comment in New Brunswick. He is evidently under the impression that when he thinks about a matter the whole public are thinking about it. The comments no doubt were limited to the hon. gentleman and his immediate party friends. It is impossible to say off-hand whether a price is unreasonable or not. We cannot very well compare the cost of dredging in one place with that of dredging in another. If my hon. friend will take up the expense per cubic yard of dredging by government dredges, he will see remarkable differences in the cost per day, depending not so much on the depth of water as on the character of the soil. You may be able to do deep dredging in many places cheaper than shallow dredging in other places. You may dredge
silt, sand or soft clay much more easily to a depth of 22 feet than harder material to a depth of seven feet.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: What was the character of dredging at Indian point?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
It would be clay. My hon. friend must bear in mind that public tenders were called for the work at Indian point. It was advertised in the daily papers at St. John, and the only tender received was that of the Maritime Dredging Company. There is another thing to be considered. If there is a large quantity of dredging to be done, extending over a period of years, such as at Fort William, you can get it done much cheaper than you can a comparatively small quantity. The dredges do not require to be moved and towed, and you can afford to invest a larger amount of capital and get more powerful dredges. At Fort William, the material is very much softer than at Indian Head. Unless you knew the exact character of the material in each place, you could not at all compare the prices. My hon. friend is in error with regard to the Maritime Dredging Company getting the same rate as Mr. Mayes. Mr. Mayes never get so low as 50 cents.	The lowest he got
was 55 cents per cubic yard, and for the greater part of the work he did at St. John he got 90 cents, and he got that after public tender. Up and down the St. Lawrence, in some cases 50, in some cases 60, and in others 70 and 75 where the dredging might not be any more difficult than at Indian point. It depends a good deal on the character of the soil. At all events, the work was let after public competition and advertisement to the Maritime Ddedgrng Company, which was the only tenderer, and on the certificate of the chief engineer that the price was veTy reasonable.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: The minister spoke about Mr. Mayes not doing any dredging as low as 50 cents. But Mr. Mayes put in a tender to do dredging at 49 cents, and it was not accepted.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
It was an irregular tender, not complying with the specifications.
Mr.' DANIEL. It was irregular simply with regard to having registered or unregistered dredge, and not with regard to the price. Then with regard to the Dominion Dredging Company, that work was not put up to public tender.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Yes it was.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Not when the Dominion Dredging Company did it.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
My hon. friend is mistaken. It was put up to public tender and Mr. Mayes tendered at 90 cents and was the

lowest. Then the Dominion Dredging Company were allowed to do part of the work at the same price.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: They were put to work without offering any tender at all.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: But at the same price as the other.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: At the same time they had a very profitable contract, as the minister knows.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: The minister does not know whether it was profitable or not. They got the same figure as the lowest tenderer.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
They got the same figure for easy work as Mr. Mayes got for difficult
work.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: It was work exactly of the same character.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: My information is that it was not. It was easier, soiter and much more profitable. They did not put in a tender but simply were given the work at the figure put in before by Mr. Mayes.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: What I said was this. Public tenders were called for the work upon the northern side of Sand Point slip. The notice was advertised in the various newspapers, tenders were received, and Mr. Mayes was the lowest, at 90 cents per cubic yard.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Was he the only tenderer?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I do not know. It was felt that he could not proceed as rapidly with the work as. public interest required and there were strong demands from the port of St. John to hasten the work. Yielding to that request, the then acting Minister of Public Works (Mr. Fisher), gave part of the work to the Dominion Dredging Company and they went on. Mr. Mayes doing a part and they the other, and both were getting 90 cents per cubic yard. Then when I became minister, I divided the work of the extension of the 400 feet extension equally. . I gave the Dominion Dredging Company the work on one side and Mr. Mayes the work on the other. The one was not any harder than the other.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I might remind the minister that Mr. Mayes found that he had to request a higher price than he was getting from his original tender because he struck a very difficult piece of dredging-a strip full of large, heavy boulders. But that strip did not extend up to the part that the Dominion Dredging Company did.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Boulders seem to breed there. After Mr. Mayes got through, we found a large number of boulders in. the vicinity of the work he had carried on. I do not know whether they breed-like the gondolas in New York.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I happened to see a plan of these boulders lying right up against the wharf, not only in the part Mr. Mayes had dredged, but where the Dominion Company had dredged as well.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: He was allowed $18.60 per yard for these boulders, though I do not think he had harder work than the Dominion Dredging Company.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
I have listened to the minister's interesting statement concerning the difficulties of dredging at Indian point.
and I feel sure that that statement, when heard by the people of the community who know the facts, will be very amusing to them.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I said it was a clay soil.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: The minister was endeavouring to justify these manifestly excessive prices paid to Mr. Moore for the dredging, on the ground that it was more difficult than at Fort William or St. John. The fact that the denth of water before dredging was three feet and that the dredging was done to a depth of seven feet will show how much reliance is to be placed in the minister's contention. As to the prices, the contract was awarded to the Dominion Dredging Company on the basis of $17 for rock or boulders exceeding two cubic yards, and 50* cents per cubic yard for all other material. The price to Mr. Mayes was $8.60 per yard for rock in the harbour of St. John, and 55 cents for other material, 5 cents of which went to the minister's friend, Mr. McAvity.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: That was the first. What was the second?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: That is the contract that was made with Mr. Mayes.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: His second contract, let at public tender, gave $19.60.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: The one in connection with which he made the agreement with the minister's friend, Mr. Geo. McAvity, whereby he agreed to pay 5 cents to Mr. McAvity for every cubic yard over 50 cents. He was willing to dredge at 50 cents a cubic yard, and entered into this agreement with Mr. McAvity to give him 5 cents a cubic yard for his influence with the government. That is all he received for doing the dredging for ordinary material in the harbour of St. John, and for rock, he was allowed $8.60. And this for dredging to a depth of 32 feet. At Indian point the minister's other friend, Mr. Moore, was to get $17 for solid rock, though it turns out there was no solid rock to be found.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Does the hon. gentleman (Mr. Crocket) say that he received anything for solid rock?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
No. But it indicates pretty well that Mr. Moore did not know

anything about the character of dredging he had undertaken to do- or the department either.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: How?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I assumed from what the minister said that when the department called for tenders, it was after an examination had been made and an estimate of cost.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: There is a uniform classification, so that, if solid rock is encountered, it is to be done at the rate.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Of $17 a cubic yard in this case?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: No, but at the rate tendered for.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: But the other material was to be paid for at 50 cents, regardless of whether it is hard or soft clay, sand or silt. I suppose the classification was the same as in other contracts. The minister spoke of doing a large quantity of dredging at a lower rate per cubic yard than would be paid for a smaller quantity, but I observe that Mr. Moore got no less than $48,247 out of what dredging was done at Maquapit lake.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Compare that with dredging at Fort William, where it will go to two or three million dollars.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: The minister says, with reference to any comment made upon this subject, that, of course, I would be speaking^ only from what I had heard from my political friends. I have been spoken to by many in New Brunswick within the last week, and asked if it could possibly be true that Mr. Moore had received $48,247 for the work done at Indian point or were the figures which were reported a mistake ? I have heard responsible citizens of St. John, some of them leading business men there who are familiar with the work, state that Mr. Moore was getting that price for dredging that was worth not more than ten cents.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Did the hon. gentleman tell these people that the work was let after public advertisement calling for tenders?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: No. I did not think that made much difference in the circumstances. The fact is that the Maritime Dredging Company got this work without competition. There may have been tenders called for

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I say there were, and by public advertisement, with the widest reasonable circulation.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: It is very singular if tenders were called for in such a way that Mr. Moore, or the Maritime Dredging Company were the only tenderers for the work in that locality and at such manifestly excessive figures.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Tenders were called for by advertisement in the usual way.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: But the minister would not give a contract if he thought the tender was too high?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I thought it a reasonable price and the chief engineer so certified.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Was any examination of the work made by the engineers of the department before tenders were called for? And was an estimate made of the cost?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: If the hon. member will look at 'Hansard' he will see that that information was given in answer to his own question.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Not concerning Indian Point?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Does the hon. gentleman say that an examination was made and an estimate prepared?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I do not know. The information is in 'Hansard.'

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I think the hon. minister is mistaken. I have the question here, and I do not remember framing any question in reference to an estimate of the cost. I think he has in mind the question relating to the wharfs.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: No; perhaps in the hon. gentleman's (Mr. Crocket's) absence the question was asked. He will find it all in 'Hansard.'

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: The minister stated just now that tenders have been asked for this Maquapit Lake dredging. Is it not a fact that the Maritime Dredging Company were put to work there before tenders were asked and that tenders were only asked for after they commenced the work and had been at it for some time?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I do not think so.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Will the minister say that that is not the case?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I think it is not the case. But, if it were the case, it would be upon this agreement-that, if they were not the lowest tenderers, they would have to leave, and that for the work they did they would have to accept the price of the lowest tenderer.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
I have been credibly informed that the Maritime Dredging Company were put to work on that dredging

some time before tenders were called for. Under these circumstances, it is altogether unnecessary to inform the minister there was good reason why there was only one tender.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: When were the tenders called for?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: We are not considering any item for that, and I would not have that information.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Would the minister bring down the information, to show when the tenders were called, and when the work was commenced?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I would be glad to do it. One word before we close, let me put this right. My hon. friend says, what is quite true, that Mr. Mayes did get one contract at 55 cents per cubic yard, and for rock for his contract was $8.60 per cubic yard. But when tenders were called for further work no more difficult than that, his tender was 90 cents per cubic yard for ordinary material, and $19.60 for rock. That was his tender, and it was in respect to that additional work on the north side of Sand point slip that the Dominion Dredging Company were allowed to do part of the work at the same price.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Was not $19.60 for solid rock and not for boulders.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
For solid rock and
boulders above two cubic yards in size. For anything above two cubic yards, he was to get $19.60 per cubic yard.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I daresay the deputy could inform the Minister, but my memory is that for ordinary soil the figure was 90 cents, and for solid rock it was $19.60, and then there was an intermediate price.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
Boulders above two
cubic yards were counted the same as solid rock. Then there was another class of boulders below two cubic yards and over half a cubic yard which was reckoned at another price.
Dredging in Ontario and Quebec, $140,000.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: How much was expended on Wingfield basin?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: It was done out of the general vote.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Is there no separate amount.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Out of this appropriation we are to use $13,521 to do the work at Wingfield basin.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Could the minister tell me if there is any town, any population at Wingfield basin? "

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Wingfield basin is a harbour of refuge, and we were strongly requested by the shipping interests to do this dredging. They regard it as an important harbour of refuge.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: To what depth has it been dredged?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I cannot say.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Who was the contractor for dredging?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: The C. C. Boone Dredging Company. It was let by public tender.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: How many tenders were there?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I cannot give that information to-night.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I am advised there was only one. What was the price?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Seventy cents per cubic yard. That would include all material except solid rock. It would include clay, hardpan, anything of that kind. There is some rock to be taken out.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Did the specifications state so much for all material except solid rock?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: When was the contract let?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: On the 26th of June, 1908.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Were tenders called for in the public newspapers?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Yes, we gave very wide circulation to the advertisement calling lor tenders.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: How much does the minister think it will take to complete?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
That would be in connection with the main estimates. This is simply to close up the business for the present year.
British Columbia - Kamloops - Okanagan telegraph system-additional amount, $1,650.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: What is this for?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
We had to provide additional wiring, and this would be the freight upon the wire.
Yukon Territory-Ashcroft-canal section of Yukon system of telegraph lines-part repoling-to complete payments, $1,206.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
A portion of the line
was found in bad condition, and we had to spend this money. It is a part of the Yukon system.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I would like to ask the minister if this is the work that was begun two or three weeks before the election in that constituency and completed two or three minutes past the election. ^

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
I do not know what particular work that was. I suppose it is not important just now.
Public Works-miscellaneous-compensation to Wm. Julien in full of all demands for injuries sustained by him on government dredge ' Ontario ' during the season of 1907, $1,000.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
This is the case of a young man who had his arm torn off while working upon the government dredge ' Ontario.' After very careful consideration we thought it proper to provide for him.
Operating and maintenance expenses-telegraph lines-Yukon system-(Ashcroft-Daw-son)-further amount required, $30,000.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: How did the minister come to be so far out in his main estimate for that line ? What is the revenue from the line ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: We have been greatly bothered in connection with the Yukon line during the past year owing to the construction of the Grand Trunk Pacific Railway. The Tailway follows our telegraph line for a long distance and in many cases wires are strung upon trees. In cutting trees wires are thrown down the sides of the mountains and we have to keep constantly at work to make repairs. We have protested to the company and the contractors and they say they have exercised all the care possible, but notwithstanding that we had to spend a great deal of money in making repairs.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Was not this due to the mode of construction of that line in the first place ? I understand that many of the poles were planted in the air and in snow banks ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I am not prepared to say that. It is a very difficult thing to build a telegraph line through the mountains of British Columbia away from highways.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: There was money enough provided not only to build one line but to build half a dozen if it had been properly spent.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: That is some time ago and I cannot give any personal explanation about it.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Would the minister answer the question as to the revenue ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: About $80,000 is the estimated revenue for the year. We have about $72,000 up to date.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Would the minister kindly inform us where the supplies for this Yukon telegraph line are procured ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Principally in Vancouver. Then we have to pack them up to the different camps. We take them up by boat to Ashcroft and pack them to the north.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Are tenders called for ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: They are bought at market rates. They have to be packed specially-

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Are they got from a wholesale firm ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: From a wholesale firm at wholesale rates.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: At retail prices.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I do not think so. They are specially put up to keep a good while, they have to be packed long distances.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Is there a patronage list in British Columbia?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: There used to be one, but I have given instructions to do away with it.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: It is still in existence?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I do not think it is. I gave directions to do away with it some time ago.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Is it not the practice of the department to call for tenders when the quantity required is as considerable as it is here?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: The department did some years ago call for tenders for supplies for this Yukon system and they got a tender from an eastern city, but the result was exceedingly unsatisfactory. A great deal of the stuff spoiled almost before it got up there and a good deal was spoiled after it reached its destination. If you get supplies into that remote country which are not perfect, if the canned meats, the cream, the milk, and butter, are not first-class and are not properly packed it is then too late to discover that they are not as they ought to be. It was found very unsatisfactory and it was decided to buy, under careful inspection, from those who could be relied upon to furnish the very best articles. This was found to give the best results.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Then am I to understand from the minister that no inspection is made of these goods when they are purchased?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Yes, an inspection is made of them and we rely more upon buying from reputable firms at fair market prices.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
Am I to understand the minister to say that he cannot get tenders

from British Columbia firms and that is the reason why tenders are not called?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: No, I did not say that, but some years ago tenders were called and the lowest tender was accepted. It proved to be very unsatisfactory and the view of the department has been that it is better to have our own superintendent make the purchase himself, get prices from reputable firms, buy from those firms, see that he only gets a good article and have the articles packed under his own supervision.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Why was it unsatisfactory?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: A good deal of the stuff spoiled.
