maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Does it affect the quality of the goods to advertise for tenders? Why should goods supplied by persons who put in tenders not be as good as those purchased from people who are not asked to submit tenders ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: If my hon. friend were going to northern British Columbia and were taking supplies for his personal use, would he call for tenders or would he go to reliable firms and get what he wanted at the lowest prices ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I would not make my purchases from one wholesale firm and pay them retail prices when I could buy from another wholesale firm at wholesale prices.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: But the hon. gentleman would not call for tenders.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: You may rest assured I would get prices from more wholesale houses than one, and I would not accept goods at retail prices when I could go half a block to another wholesale house and get the same goods at wholesale prices. Will the minister tell me now whether he has purchased any goods for this telegraph system from any but one firm in British Columbia ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I did go very carefully into the bills for goods supplied for this Yukon system and I got my deputy to get prices for similar goods in Ottawa, and I had explanations with regard to the different items, and I satisfied myself that the prices were fair and reasonable and were wholesale prices.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Did you do that in the case of all the goods you purchased ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I took the goods running over a certain number of months.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Does the minister vouch for the fact that the prices charged were wholesale prices and were not retail prices or higher than retail prices ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: In the particular bills I examined I was satisfied they were fair wholesale prices.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
For what year were these
bills ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Last year or the year before.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: All the bills ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: No, the bills which came from one firm in Vancouver.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: What firm was that ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Is there a firm called Kelly, Douglas & Company?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Oh. yes, there isn't any other.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: In what year did the minister call for tenders ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: It was when the late Mr. Tarte was Minister of Public Works.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: The minister has admitted that the supplies for this telegraph line are purchased practically altogether from one firm in Vancouver and without calling for tenders.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: There is no public call for tenders.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: The minister admits that pratically all the business has been done with Kelly, Douglas & _ Company and I suppose he knows that this particular firm has an exceedingly strong affiliation with the Liberal party; in fact that it has been the mainspring of the Liberal party for many years. It is regarded as a very strong grievance throughout British Columbia that these rather important supplies for telegraph lines in the north all go to this particular firm and that .other firms in British Columbia have not a chance of participating in that business. It has caused a great deal of adverse public criticism and it is looked upon as a reward for political services rendered from time to time. There are other firms outside of those in Vancouver who could furnish these supplies to the government and I might mention the Reid firm at Quesnel which does business at the very point from which these telegraph lines start. Whenever any other than the Kelly, Douglas firm, in British Columbia has endeavoured to get this business they have been told; you will have to see the member. I would like to have to-night some assurance from the minister that in future other firms in British Columbia will have an opportunity to compete for these telegraph supplies. It would be in the interest of the government itself if an end were put to the present system. I can assure the minister that the present system is almost in the nature of a scandal and were it unearthed to the bottom I quite believe there would be some startling disclosures.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
I am very much in favour of giving different firms an opportunity

of tendering, because I realize that in that way we are apt to get goods at the lowest price. There is some difference between buying goods for use right in the city where the goods are used, and, purchasing supplies of butter and canned meats, and condensed milk, and desiccated apples to be sent to distant territory into the wilderness. I can understand how, if the department has been getting perfect satisfaction from this firm for a number of years there would be a disposition to continue trading with them, just as people continue for years dealing with the Hudson's Bay Company because they have the reputation of always carrying out their contracts to the letter. I have no doubt there are other firms in Vancouver who would do the business equally well, but I suppose there has been a disposition not to change when satisfaction has been given. I intend to look into this question in British Columbia as elsewhere, and my disposition is to have all the supplies for the department obtained as far as possible by public competition. I can assure my hon. friend that that matter will receive careful consideration.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Then we can feel confident that the minister proposes to do away with the patronage system in British Columbia?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: The patronage list has been done away with already.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Well this firm-Kelly Bouglas is it?-has been getting all the custom of the government in the Public Works Department since 1896. Is that correct?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
I do not know as to 'that.
Mr. _ COWAN. Sines the minister has been in charge of thi3 department, Kelly, Douglas & Company have been getting all its custom?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I cannot say that; no.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: On this Yukon line, I believe I heard the minister say?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I said that the accounts I examined were accounts of Kelly, Douglas & Company.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: And you know of no other accounts?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: These are the only accounts I examined. There are a good many and I wanted to go into the items very particularly.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Would the minister not think it might possibly be in the public interest if an inquiry were made as to whether other firms are getting any part of the custom of his department and as to whether their prices may not be a shade better than Kelly-Douglas'?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: If I thought their prices were a shade better and .their goods of ns high quality I would certainly buy from others.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Will the minister give the committee an assurance that before he gives any further orders, he will ascertain from the other firms what their prices are ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I will give that due consideration; yes.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
And give the committee
the assurance that other firms will be given an opportunity of tendering on the next order?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I think I have given a very satisfactory assurance to my hon. friend.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
I have had a number of very satisfactory assurances, but I am
speaking now of one particular assurance. I think the committee would be glad if the minister would assure them that the next order of his department will be open to tender from all the houses having the goods needed, and that a careful comparison of prices will be made and the best man get the order.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: My hon. friend can rest assured that I will not make any purchases except at fair and reasonable prices.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
But always from Kelly-
Douglas.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: No, not always.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Will the minister be good enough to assure this committee that some one else than Kelly-Douglas will have an opportunity of tendering on the next order?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I can assure my hon. friend that I will give no contract to any one that will not give us the goods at the very lowest market price. How does that strike the hon. gentleman?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I regret that that assurance is scarcely what I consider to be in the public interest. I think it is a clever assurance, but I doubt if it is in the public interest, and I doubt if the public will take it as in their interest. I believe that the public want business done by the department of the minister as a sane, honest business man would do his own business.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Hear, hear, that is right.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
And I believe that a sane, honest business man would not give all his orders to one firm without calling for tenders and inquiring for prices or inspecting the goods before delivery. I do not think that is the act of a sane, honest business man in the conduct of his own business, and I believe that this committee has the right to the assurance I am asking from the minister that in future orders will be open to tender to other firms than that of Kelly-Douglas. We know who Kelly-Doug-las are, we know who Kelly is, the minister knows, we all know. We know that he makes the political appointments through-

out the whole provinse of British Columbia for this government.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Is he Irish?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: His name would indicate that. We all know that we are only trifling when we are calling him Kelly-Douglas; we know who Kelly-Douglas is and the people of British Columbia will say that I am perfectly right in asking in a polite way that the minister will give us some assurance that some one else than Kelly-Douglas will have a chance at the patronage of this department.	[DOT]

speakerposition: Minister of Mines; Minister of Inland Revenue
maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I do not particularly take exception to the request of my hon. friend from Vancouver (Mr. Cowan) that the Minister of Public Works should intimate to the House his decision to have public competition if that is his policy; but I do take exception to the implication rather than the direct assurance of my hon. friend from Vancouver (Mr. Cowan), that Kelly Douglas & Company have been in any way overcharging the department. Neither my hon. friend from Vancouver (Mr. Cowan) nor my hon. friend from Yale-Cariboo (Mr. Burrell) has stated this to be the case. If they know that Kelly Douglas & Company have been overcharging the department, they ought to say so. Kelly, Douglas & Company is one of the largest wholesale grocery firms in British Columbia, in fact, in Canada. The firm do a business of several million dollars a year.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: The hon. gentleman knows that before Kelly-Douglas got the account of the Dominion government, Bob Kelly was not worth $ 1,400. He knows that as well as I do.

speakerposition: Minister of Mines; Minister of Inland Revenue
maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I do not know anything of the kind. I am not here as an advocate of Mr. Robert Kelly, the. principal partner of the firm of Kelly, Douglas & Company, who is certainly a thorn in the flesh of my hon. friend from Vancouver (Mr. Cowan). I do not know what prices he has charged the department. I do not know whether he has tendered or not. My hon. friend has not criticised the prices, he does not know himself whether the department has been overcharged for anything; there is simply the desire on the part of my hon. friend to attack a very prominent citizen of the city of Vancouver, who is at the same time a very prominent and active politician, Robert Kelly of the firm of Kelly Douglas & Company. If it is a fact that the firm is overcharging I am with my hon. friend and would request the Minister of Public Works to see that the public is not overcharged, whether he does it by public competition or not. -Mr. COWAN.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: There is no pretence of anything of the kind.

speakerposition: Minister of Mines; Minister of Inland Revenue
maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: My hon. friend has said that public appointments in British Columbia are now made by Robert Kelly. That is not true, that is not accurate to be strictly parliamentary, and my hon. friend knows that very well. Mr. Robert Kelly is an active politician, as everybody in Vancouver knows, he is a very prominent citizen, he is one of the most successful men, in a business way, in Vancouver.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Since he got the government account.

speakerposition: Minister of Mines; Minister of Inland Revenue
maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: The government ac-cout is a mere bagatelle in his business. All he got is the grocery and provision supplies on the Yukon telegraph line. It is probably an extraordinary thing for one minister to suggest a matter of patronage to another minister. Here is the member for the city of Vancouver who is not satisfied that these goods, whether the amount be a thousand dollars or fifty thousand dollars, should be purchased in his city. Well, I wish to say to my hon. colleague, the Minister of Public Works, that I represent Comox-Atlin, the capital of which is Prince Rupert, that Prince Rupert is on the line of the Yukon Telegraph, and Vancouver is not, and therefore to please the member of Vancouver if the department transferred its orders to the city of Prince Rupert.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I would be delighted to see that patronage go to wherever there' would be a saving for the Dominion.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I want to emphasize again the point-and it not only affects Vancouver-that public tenders should be invited in all cases. The telegraph line starts in the lower portion of my constituency, and the minister should give an opportunity to the dealers in that portion to tender for these supplies.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I would ask the Minister of Inland Revenue (Mr. Temple-man) to take down the figures as I give them from the Auditor General's Report and he will see what they amount to. maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Who administers the patronage of the hon. minister's department at Vancouver ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: The purchases are made by the agent of the department in Vancouver. The superintendent of the Yukon Telegraph Line, Mr. Phelan, makes the purchases for the Yukon telegraph, and Mr. Keefer, the resident engineer, for the use of the dredges.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Are they instructed to purchase from Kelly, Douglas & Company?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: They are instructed to make their purchases at fair prices. I have given no directions to purchase from Kelly, Douglas & Company.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: In the interest of clean administration and in order to get rid of disagreeable suspicions, would it not be well for the minister to give some assurance that tenders will be called for and other firms given an opportunity to tender for the supplies of his department. There seems to be only one name on the patronage list.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Then it ought not to be difficult to destroy it.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: But the smaller the list, the more difficult it seems to be to destroy it. I think it would be very much in the interest of clean administration. It would have a very beneficial effect upon the public opinion of that country. It would lead them to think that Mr. Kelly had not the minister's department in his pocket.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I have already said, and it has been publicly announced, that we have done away with the patronage list in our department, and that purchasing agents have already had instructions to get prices from different dealers.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: And, in Vancouver, they are not confined to Kelly, Douglas & Company.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: They are quite open to go to any dealer. Mr. Phelan has instructions to get prices from different people. These instructions went out a considerable time ago.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: That is, instructions with regard to these supplies-

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: These instructions apply to all supplies!

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: The instructions that apply to these particular supplies-are they, or are they not, in writing?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: This item applies to the current year before the patronage list was abolished.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: My question seemed to me to be rather plain. Are these instructions in writing?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Carried.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Perhaps I have not made myself understood. Are the instructions to purchasing agents to get prices from other firms in Vancouver than Kelly, Douglas & Company in writing ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Carried.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I am waiting for an answer by the minister.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I must apologize-what was the question?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I understood from the minister that instructions had been given to the purchasing agent, Mr. Taylor, to get prices from firms other than Kelly, Douglas & Company for the supplies needed for this line. I ask if the instructions are in writing?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I did not say that. I said that instructions of a general character had been issued, directing the purchasing agent to be careful to employ competent men, careful as to the prices at which they purchased goods, to get the goods at lowest market rates, and to inspect them- to do everything to make sure that value was got for the money.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Have these instructions been given to Mr. Taylor?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: To all the agents. There is no Mr. Taylor.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Who is the purchasing agent?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Mr. Phelan.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Has he received written instructions to get prices from other firms than Kelly, Douglas & Company?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
His instructions are general-to get goods at the lowest market, prices irrespective of any particular firm.
Mr. 'COWAN. Are these instructions in writing?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: A circular has gone out.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: To Mr. Phelan?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: To all the agents.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Can the minister bring down a copy of these written instructions?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
I shall be glad to do
so.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: When were these instructions given?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: About three months ago.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Then, we may hope that prices will be obtained from firms other, than Kelly, Douglas & Company.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: We may hope that- yes.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Will the minister assure the committee that prices will be got from ether firms than Kelly, Douglas and Company?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Yes, no doubt.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: And that, before the order is given to Kelly, Douglas & Company, prices will be got from other firms?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: That is the duty of Mr. Phelan.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
According to the_ written instructions, which the minister will bring
dawn?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I do not want to bore the committee, but if I am in order, 1 would like to refer for a moment to the carriage of these supplies. On March 3, I put the question on the paper in connection with the carrying of these supplies up on the telegraph lines. I would impress upon the minister that the same policy I am advocating now, which every hon. member ought to sympathize with, the policy of public tender, should be carried out in connection with the carriage of goods as well as the purchase of them. It is a very big contract. It was given in 1901, the minister stated, in answer to an advertisement, for tender published in the town of Hazelton. Strong complaint is made throughout the north end of my riding that tenders were not asked for in the usual way. A small notice was given in Hazelton and none of those in the Cariboo country, where the supplies start, knew anything about it. The contract was let at 17i cents per pound for carrying the supplies. They get that price, even "if they do carry the goods eight miles. And this in the face of the fact that, years ago, contractors were taking supplies for the Hudson Bay Company all through that country under more difficult circumstances, at five cents and six cents a pound, and were making money. I do not wish to assume jthat the, minister would wish to continue a state of things that is more or less a scandal in that north country. I hope that the minister will arrange to have contracts given after notice calling for tender. If he does so, he will get this work done at a lower figure than at present

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: It follows from the doing away with the patronage list that we must-have competition for carying supplies, for that is part of the cost of the supplies to the country. I have already given directions to the officials of my department that tenders shall be called for packing of these goods into northern British Columbia.

speakerposition: Minister of Mines; Minister of Inland Revenue
maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I dispute the assertion of the hon. member for Yale-Cariboo (Mr. Burrell) that goods can be packed into the interior of that country for five cents a pound.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext: I was talking last summer to a gentleman who was discussing this question, and he told me that he stood on the shores of Stewart lake and saw a packer who had packed a heavy amount of freight from Ashcroft up to Stewart lake and delivered it at that point, at 8 cents a pound, and made money. It is known all through that country, and if there is one thing that is a particular reproach to the government it has been carrying these supplies year by year without a renewal of tender, at what is conceded, even by his own Liberal friends, to be an extravagant price.

speakerposition: Minister of Mines; Minister of Inland Revenue
maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
I disnute the accuracy of my hon. friend's statements. To say that goods can be carried from Ashcroft to Barkerville and further, all through a wilderness, by trails and where there are no trails, for 8 cents a pound, is to my mind an absolute absurdity.

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
This is a claim for interest, and arises in connection with the construction of that large pier at Montreal called Maisonneuve pier. When the work was built there was a dispute between the 'government and the contractors as to a certain claim, and it was finally left to a departmental board of referees, consisting of the chief engineer, the deputy minister, and the engineer of the Ottawa river works. After hearing the evidence they awarded to the contractors a considerable sum against the government. That amount was paid, and this is for interest at 5 per cent from the time when the work was done, as found by the referees, to the time of payment.
' Mr. LENNOX. Was the claim reduced?

maintopic: SUPPLY-INTERCOLONIAL RAILWAY FREIGHT CLERKS, HALIFAX AND ST. JOHN.
speechtext:
The claim was reduced. The amount of interest is about $25,000.
